articles.title: 'No signs US strikes trigger Iran blasts'
articles.excerpt: Iranian media suggested explosions in southern Iran on Saturday evening were related to Iranian military activities rather than US strikes…
articles.fullText:
Iranian media suggested explosions in southern Iran on Saturday evening were related to Iranian military activities rather than US strikes while both sides reported that shipping had been hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran's state television said officials had not confirmed any missile strikes on Iranian territory following blasts heard in several areas, including on Qeshm Island in the strait.

US President Donald Trump had hinted at renewing major attacks on Iran after ⁠last week's midterm elections but there has been no sign of a large-scale US military operation, which Iran has said it would respond to by striking US and Israeli targets.

Both sides have continued strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, however, restricting exports of energy and other commodities vital to the world economy.

Iran's state television said the evening explosions might be related to Iranian military activity in the waterway, where Iran said two vessels had hit mines and a third had caught fire.

The US said its air force had disabled a vessel in the Gulf of Oman beyond the strait.

Tasnim news agency said two missiles had struck Qeshm Island, with no official information on possible damage. Neither Iran nor the US has commented on that report. Washington said on November 2 that it had struck the island in a limited defensive measure against Iranians using surface-to-air missiles against US assets.

Since the US and Israel began attacks on Iran in February, Tehran has sought the upper hand by hitting vessels in the Strait of Hormuz to block Gulf energy exports, while US forces began blockading movements to and from Iranian ports in April.

The US military said on Saturday evening that its air force had fired at the stern of a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman, disabling it as it tried to get through the blockade.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said two oil tankers had caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to pass through an "unauthorised route" in the Strait of Hormuz. A third tanker had also suffered an explosion and caught fire, the semi-official Fars news agency reported later.

Reuters was not able to confirm any of the reported strikes.

Meanwhile, a conflict between Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen and Saudi Arabia has escalated this month, enlarging the wider Middle East war.

On Sunday, Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said an administrative building belonging to state oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh had been damaged by falling debris after an attempted attack, with no injuries or fatalities reported.

Qatar, which has been mediating in talks to try to end the conflict that has shaken the world economy, on Saturday denied reports that the US and Iran had failed to reach a deal.

The Qatari prime minister had affirmed that both sides were continuing to ⁠work towards an agreement.

Iran has submitted a nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Thursday, saying the US was reviewing it but discussions would depend on Washington first meeting Tehran's seven demands.

These include sanctions relief, access to frozen assets and war reparations, while Washington insists nuclear issues must feature in initial talks.

On Saturday, the US military said it was launching a task force to crack down on the movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material to Iran via its land borders and the Caspian Sea – part of economic measures to try to pressure Tehran.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards dismissed the plan as "wordplay", saying it would not work because Tehran had made preparations and communicated closely with its neighbours. (Reuters)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Pope Leo wraps up Uruguay visit, Argentina next
articles.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV wrapped up his visit to Uruguay on Sunday by marking an important Catholic feast day that is…
articles.fullText:
Pope Leo XIV wrapped up his visit to Uruguay on Sunday by marking an important Catholic feast day that is tied to the country’s independence, capping his effort to draw attention to the role the church played in the founding of Latin America’s most secular country.

Leo travelled to the city of Florida, north of Montevideo, before heading to Argentina for the second leg of his three-nation tour of South America.

It's expected to be the most politically delicate, given the Catholic Church's sharp criticisms of the austerity programme of libertarian President Javier Milei.

For his final event in Uruguay, Leo was commemorating the feast of the Virgin of the Thirty-three. Every year, thousands of pilgrims flock to Florida on the second Sunday of every November to pray before the small wooden icon of the Virgin Mary housed there.

According to tradition, 33 independence patriots acquired the Guaraní statue and had it with them when independence was declared from the Brazilian empire in Florida on August 25, 1825.

Leo became the first pope in nearly four decades to visit Uruguay, in hopes of reminding its people that the Catholic Church is part of their very identity as a nation – even if in subsequent decades the country went on a deeply secular, and at times anticlerical, route.

Thousands of people poured into Florida's main square on Sunday ahead of the Mass under brilliant blue skies, some walking for several kilometres to reach the site.

Leo was hoping to leave a parting message before opening the second leg of his South American trip, which he went ahead with despite having undergone surgery on October 13 to remove a cancerous tumour from his lung.

The final stop is in Peru, his second homeland.

Leo, 71, has appeared in fine form at his events, singing loudly, bounding up stairs and gamely greeting the crowds in his popemobile. He has not cut any events short, including those that have kept him out until past midnight Rome time.

“This visit will also serve to reinforce the image of Leo as a leader, not merely in a spiritual sense, but in a much broader capacity as a political leader and a widely recognised figure who, far from shying away from conflict or tension, offers a powerful perspective and commands a highly respected voice,” said Luis Bahamondes, a professor at the Center for Judaic Studies at the University of Chile.

In Buenos Aires, Milei is due to greet Leo at the airport and then the two will appear together for the traditional welcome ceremony and exchange of speeches. The encounter could be tense, given the Catholic Church's criticism of Milei’s austerity measures that have slashed social spending, and his embrace of artificial intelligence.

Milei has staked his presidency on cutting social spending to overhaul Argentina’s troubled economy and deliver a long-elusive budget surplus. He has called social justice “an aberration” that amounts to stealing, and mocked as “huge stupidity” the increasingly common complaint in Argentina that families squeezed by his austerity programme can’t make it to the end of the month.

Leo, who took his name from the 19th-century pope whose encyclical on labour laid the foundation of Catholic social teaching, has made the poor and vulnerable a focus of his papacy, carrying on the legacy of his Argentine predecessor, Pope Francis.

In Argentina, Leo is completing unfinished business left by his predecessor. The Argentine Jesuit, the former archbishop of Buenos Aires, never returned home during his 12-year pontificate, confounding friends and foes alike. (AP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: 'France to represent Europe at Russia-Ukraine talks'
articles.excerpt: Europe will be represented at upcoming US-mediated talks with Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the Ukraine…
articles.fullText:
Europe will be represented at upcoming US-mediated talks with Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the Ukraine war, France said on Sunday.

"The Europeans will be represented and France will be in Abu Dhabi to participate in these talks," French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot told RTL radio.

His comment came after President Donald Trump stoked fears of a US pivot towards the Kremlin by predicting a "very big" deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but "all of Europe".

Up to now, the talks scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday had been framed as a trilateral format at the level of officials, not leaders, from Ukraine, Russia and the United States.

The identities of who would take part have not been made public.

Although Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has made it clear that he wants involvement from European allies in the process, Russia has suggested there would be no place for European representatives at the table.

Barrot said that, in the past, "there have been discussions, sometimes without the Europeans and sometimes with" but "this time they will participate".

He said: "France will be there and will ensure that Europe's voice is heard."

On Thursday, US, European, Ukrainian and Nato officials met in Brussels ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks.

A Nato spokeswoman said they "sought to advance a just and sustainable end to the war in Ukraine".

Jared Kushner, the US president's envoy and son-in-law, participated in the Brussels meeting by videolink. He said the United States was working on "a broader European security architecture that can help establish the conditions for lasting peace".

The American approach is being treated warily by European allies, which have long rejected Moscow's desire to rewrite the European security architecture.

Before launching the war in Ukraine in 2022, the Kremlin delivered an ultimatum to Nato which included a demand that the alliance's troops be withdrawn from eastern Europe.

That was rejected by the Western military alliance.

Kushner on Thursday said that Washington will "consult closely with our European partners on the sidelines" of the Abu Dhabi talks and "if progress is made, aim to move toward a broader multilateral format with their direct participation". (AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Liu overpowers Eala for HK Open crown
articles.excerpt: Claire Liu of the United States powered to victory at the Hong Kong Tennis Open on Sunday, dismantling Philippine sensation…
articles.fullText:
Claire Liu of the United States powered to victory at the Hong Kong Tennis Open on Sunday, dismantling Philippine sensation Alexandra Eala 6-3, 6-0 for her maiden tour-level singles title.

Liu, who entered the WTA 250 event ranked 102nd in the world, added the SAR trophy to a cabinet which already includes challenger-level titles she won in Paris in 2022 and in Barranquilla in September this year.

The pair found themselves locked in a fierce battle at Victoria Park early on, trading blistering shots to go level at 3-3 in the opening set.

After the second-seeded Eala received medical treatment on her right knee, Liu began to pull away convincingly, capitalising on costly errors from her opponent to claim the opener in 38 minutes while overcoming a strong show of support from Filipino fans in the crowd.

The second set proved to be a far more straightforward affair, with Liu breaking serves and wearing out a visibly shaken-up Eala to take the title in dominant fashion.

"This week in general has been really fun," Liu told reporters after her win.

"But it's also been mentally really tough... last tournament of the year, it's a really big push.

"I was just trying to take it one day at a time, and I found myself in the finals."

She also spoke about having to shake off nerves prior to the championship match.

"You really want to win no matter what," she added. "But I think I was just trying to make it like it's just one other match, and yeah, it worked out."

Defeat denied a second major career title for Eala, who was bidding to add to her historic triumph in Washington DC in August that saw her become the first Filipina player to reach and win a WTA 500 final.

Still, Eala spoke highly of the support shown to her in the SAR.

"The fans are amazing, and they add another dimension to my job and to my life that beforehand I could not even imagine," Eala said.

"Thanks to them I'm able to have such special experiences and create such amazing memories, so I'm super, super happy for their support."

In the doubles final, Japan’s Miyu Kato and Chinese Taipei’s Chan Hao-Ching claimed the title, beating Talia Gibson and Maddison Inglis of Australia 6-4, 6-4.

articles.title: Dozens hurt in central Japan tremor
articles.excerpt: A strong 5.7-magnitude earthquake shook central Japan early on Sunday, injuring dozens of people, shattering windows and disrupting train services…
articles.fullText:
A strong 5.7-magnitude earthquake shook central Japan early on Sunday, injuring dozens of people, shattering windows and disrupting train services, officials and local media said.

The quake struck at 1.04am in Shizuoka Prefecture, west of Tokyo, the Japan Meteorological Agency said.

No tsunami warning was issued.

Authorities reported no deaths, but the quake shattered storefront windows and knocked items off shelves and caused transport disruption in parts of the country.

An emergency official in Aichi told AFP authorities had received 16 reports of mostly minor injuries.

Authorities in neighbouring Shizuoka said at least three women sought emergency medical care, including a woman in her nineties who injured her shoulder after falling from her bed during the shaking.

The local Chunichi Shimbun newspaper and Tokai Television separately reported at least 24 were hurt across the two regions.

In Toyohashi city in the Aichi region, windows of a car dealership were found shattered after the quake.

A large bookstore in Toyota city, also in Aichi, reported that its merchandise dropping from shelves.

The quake also forced temporary delays and suspensions of regional train services on Sunday morning, including the Shinkansen bullet trains.

It was felt as far west as Osaka, where a foreign resident was taken to hospital after falling from a second-floor apartment when the shaking startled them, local media reported.

Separately, a 4.3-magnitude quake struck the Kumamoto region at 10.53am on Sunday, the Meteorological Agency said.

There were no immediate reports of serious damage or injuries from the second quake.

The southwestern region is still trying to recover from a 7.1-magnitude tremor that killed 38 people, flattened homes and left tens of thousands without power in July. (AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: New buildings body to recruit about 90 staff: Linn
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn said the Building Maintenance Support and Services Council plans to recruit around 90 people in…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn said the Building Maintenance Support and Services Council plans to recruit around 90 people in the initial phase.

The government announced the formation of the new body in the wake of the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire last year, and it aims to help homeowners with building maintenance and renovation works. The council will be set up by the end of the year, offering a paid service to handle tendering and evaluation on their behalf.

Speaking on a TV programme on Sunday, Linn said the new staff will include professionals, technical staff, as well as support and administrative personnel.

"We want to begin recruitment now so that new hires can be onboard as quickly as possible, and the goal is to have all these staff join in phases and be fully in place between the beginning and the middle of next year."

On whether to adopt the two-envelope approach for projects – which assesses the technical aspects and the price separately – the development minister said that could apply to more complex projects.

And she doesn't believe it would raise the price tag.

"The two-envelope system mainly depends on the weighting which is predetermined, and ultimately, quality is guaranteed, and it won't drive up prices as a result."

Linn noted that penalties and spot checks would be strengthened, and will not rule out the possibility of introducing a demerit points system in the future.

Separately, she said more than 1,000 training-related applications had been approved under the Construction Innovation and Technology Fund as of September.

The government established the fund in 2018, entrusting the Construction Industry Council to finance construction technology training programmes for companies and organisations.

Writing in a blog post, Linn said the total funding amount reached HK$50 million, benefiting more than 400 companies and organisations.

She noted that more than 4,500 people have enrolled in courses offered by the Construction Industry Council over the past three years.

The development chief stressed her bureau will continue to promote local training and drive the use of technology to raise overall construction productivity.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Three hurt after hit by landing paraglider
articles.excerpt: Three people were injured on Sunday after being struck by a paraglider that was trying to land at the Ngong…
articles.fullText:
Three people were injured on Sunday after being struck by a paraglider that was trying to land at the Ngong Ping campsite at Ma On Shan Country Park.

Police said they received a report shortly after 12.30pm from a 42-year-old woman, who said she had been knocked down by a paraglider piloted by a man.

Her son and another youngster, aged 14 and 15 respectively, were also hit.

Officers said the trio sustained head and back injuries and were airlifted by the Government Flying Service to hospital for treatment.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Govt to boost high-value tourism and Mice
articles.excerpt: Financial Secretary Paul Chan on Sunday said the government would continue to support the growth of high-value tourism alongside the…
articles.fullText:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan on Sunday said the government would continue to support the growth of high-value tourism alongside the Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions (Mice) industry.

Writing in his weekly blog, Chan noted that Hong Kong had been buzzing with major events over the past week, including financial summits and international exhibitions.

He highlighted the three-day inaugural "Festival of Connoisseurs", which showcased an array of luxury goods such as supercars, yachts and jewellery, noting that it drew over 3,000 visitors from around the world.

Citing industry research, Chan said visitors attending international exhibitions spend an average of HK$9,300 per person, which is 70 percent higher than a typical overnight tourist.

The research, he said, also estimated that the exhibition industry contributed over HK$50 billion to Hong Kong’s economy in 2024 and created around 67,000 full-time jobs.

Chan said the government would continue to vigorously promote mega events across different fields and improve supporting facilities.

The Tourism Board, he added, would also continue to work with the industry to tailor more unique experiences and services for high-value visitors.

Looking ahead, Chan noted that Hong Kong's capacity for large-scale Mice events would expand by more than 40 percent upon the completion of Phase 2 of AsiaWorld-Expo and the Wan Chai North redevelopment project.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: DOJ eyes closer ties with legal sector for global push
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Justice Paul Lam on Sunday said the government hoped to work closely with the legal sector to help…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Justice Paul Lam on Sunday said the government hoped to work closely with the legal sector to help practitioners better navigate the changing international environment and strengthen external exchanges.

Speaking on a Commercial Radio programme, Lam stressed that collaboration was a central theme of this year’s Legal Week, which concluded on Friday, demonstrating the government's drive to take the initiative.

"The Department of Justice often plays a leading role. We hope that more of our local friends from the legal sector will participate, understand the latest environment, and make new connections — whether from the mainland or overseas. Internally, we must collaborate, but more importantly, we need to collaborate with partners outside Hong Kong," he said.

For Hong Kong to truly live up to its reputation as an international legal centre, the justice secretary stressed the SAR needs to strengthen relationships with external legal institutions and engage in more direct communication.

Describing it as “symbolic”, Lam noted that the International Institute for the Unification of Private Law held its centenary celebration in Hong Kong during Legal Week while concurrently hosting the opening ceremony for its Asia-Pacific Liaison Office.

He stressed that Hong Kong secured the institution's first office outside its seat in Rome in its 100-year history with the country's support.

He added that Hong Kong played an important role in helping the nation promote a fairer, and rules-based international order.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Impeached Paraguay leader charged over bank implosion
articles.excerpt: Paraguayan prosecutors charged ex-president Santiago Pena and took him into custody on Saturday over a banking crisis that saw millions…
articles.fullText:
Paraguayan prosecutors charged ex-president Santiago Pena and took him into custody on Saturday over a banking crisis that saw millions cut off from their money and sparked major protests.

Pena, Paraguay's youngest-ever president, was removed from office by the Senate on Friday, just three days after the collapse of a leading bank with which he had business links.

He had offered to resign but lawmakers impeached him instead, thereby stripping him of the immunity he would have enjoyed had he stepped down.

In a fast-moving sequence of events, he was brought before prosecutors on Saturday and charged with "breach of trust and mismanagement for personal gain."

After a hearing with Pena, Judge Hernan Otazu told reporters he had ordered the former president taken into pre-trial custody and held at the same Asuncion facility where he was taken after his removal from office on Friday.

An indictment against Pena states that "between 2023 and 2026, UENO BANK S.A. allegedly received deposits and loans from public and pension entities" and that it "was also allegedly granting loans to companies linked to the bank's economic group in an irregular manner."

Pena was grilled for around three hours over his links to Ueno Bank, a digital-first fintech company with which nearly half of Paraguay's population of 6.5 million have accounts.

The 47-year-old economist owned shares in Ueno Holding, the controlling company of the bank, until he sold them last year.

Prosecutors asked that his assets and those of former Central Bank president Carlos Carvallo, who is charged with the same offences, be frozen.

During the hearing Pena declined to make a statement, Otazu said.

Pena spent Friday night in custody after being arrested within an hour of his lightning-fast Senate impeachment trial.

Protesters gathered outside his home to demand he be locked up in a regular prison.

"We want to see the person responsible for this tragedy in jail. Jail for Pena!" Macarena Chilavert, a 33-year-old lawyer, told AFP near the prosecutor's office.

Pena was replaced by former vice president Pedro Alliana, who promised not to abandon the almost three million depositors, including pensioners, affected by Ueno's demise.

On the streets of Asuncion there was rejoicing over Pena's ouster.

But the news that Alliana, who is from the same right-wing Colorado Party, would take over angered some demonstrators.

"He's from the same team, he knew about it (the trouble at Ueno)," Edson Vazquez told AFP.

The collapse of Ueno, which handled the accounts of several state entities as well as state pensions, rocked usually stable Paraguay.

Thousands of people took to the streets furiously demanding their money back after the Central Bank took control of Ueno, citing fears for its solvency.

The Central Bank said it had begun making advance payments to an unspecified number of depositors.

Pena's removal is a further blow for US President Donald Trump's network of allies in South America.

Trump's favourite for Brazilian president, Flavio Bolsonaro, was defeated by left-wing incumbent Lula Inacio Lula da Silva last month.

Alliana will serve out the remainder of Pena's term, which ends in 2028.

Writing on X Saturday, Juan Pablo Segura, US assistant secretary of state for Western hemisphere affairs, called Paraguay a "strategic partner, friend and ally of the United States" and said Washington looked forward to working with Alliana. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Trump accuses Democrats of 'extortion'
articles.excerpt: US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that Democrat threats to use their incoming majority in Congress to impeach members…
articles.fullText:
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that Democrat threats to use their incoming majority in Congress to impeach members of his administration amounted to "extortion."

Trump faces a radically transformed and hostile political landscape after Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate in Tuesday's midterms.

Democrats have vowed investigations into Trump and senior members of his administration, including Attorney General Todd Blanche and Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth.

"The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people," Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform.

"This is extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable," he said, arguing that there had been "no impeachable acts committed."

With control of committees in both chambers, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, potentially putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny.

Likely subjects include the Trump family's business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war.

Democrats have also signalled interest in the handling of files relating to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

The administration could resist demands for testimony or documents, triggering court battles.

Democrats could pursue Trump's third impeachment, though party leaders have not committed to doing so.

The House needs only a simple majority to impeach, but removing a president requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate — far beyond the party's numbers. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Israel president taps Eisenkot to form new government
articles.excerpt: Israel's president announced on Saturday he would task Gadi Eisenkot with forming the next government following last week's election, in…
articles.fullText:
Israel's president announced on Saturday he would task Gadi Eisenkot with forming the next government following last week's election, in what Benjamin Netanyahu's rivals see as a first step to remove the country's longest-serving prime minister.

The opposition bloc led by Eisenkot, a former military chief and political newcomer who has tried to appeal to secular and liberal Israelis, has opened the door to a once improbable alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jews, which could give it the numbers to form a coalition.

President Isaac Herzog said that after consultations with all parties during the week, he would grant Eisenkot the first chance to form a government after the October 27 election, in which neither side secured a majority in a country deeply polarised by Netanyahu's hard-right rule and worn down by three years of war.

The formal appointment would take place in an official ceremony on Sunday at the president's residence in Jerusalem, Herzog's office said.

Eisenkot, who later pledged to "do everything" to form a new government, was recommended by parties representing 67 lawmakers as opposed to 46 for Netanyahu's bloc.

But the recommendations for Eisenkot included members of Israel's Arab minority — whose seat haul soared in the election on the back of anger against Netanyahu — and right-leaning segments of the opposition that are against relying on Arab votes.

Herzog, originally from Israel's now defunct left-wing Labour Party, but who has a non-partisan role and has forged a working relationship with Netanyahu, has signalled that he would like to explore a national unity government that would seek to bring together Jewish Israelis from across the political spectrum.

Pressure for a unity government could build if Netanyahu follows through on threats to resume war on Iran, although US President Donald Trump has not given the green light.

Netanyahu, who has led Israel on and off for nearly two decades and guided its sharply rightward turn in recent years, faces corruption charges and potentially jail if he leaves office.

He also faces an arrest warrant over the Gaza war from the International Criminal Court, whose authority he rejects.

Netanyahu has already called for a unity government, but the opposition has stood firm on removing him first.

He has attacked opposition leaders for even considering working with Israeli Arabs, descendants of Palestinians who stayed after the creation of Israel in 1948.

The incumbent premier said on Saturday that a potential coalition between opposition parties and Arab lists, which he called Islamists, would "dismantle the State of Israel from within" and urged the formation of a unity government comprising "all the Zionist parties that want to safeguard our state."

In response, Eisenkot's Yashar Party urged Netanyahu's allies and members of his Likud Party to form a unity government led by Eisenkot and to "publicly announce the dissolution of their alliance with the extremists".

"Now is the time to form a national emergency government," Eisenkot wrote on X in his first reaction to the announcement of his designation.

"I will do everything to ensure we are worthy."

Opposition bloc member Avigdor Liberman, a former Netanyahu aide turned fierce critic who nonetheless shares his hawkish views on the Palestinians, has made clear that he will not sit with Eisenkot if he relies on Israeli-Arab votes.

But on Friday, Liberman — a staunch secularist whose support base initially was Russian-speaking immigrants — made a U-turn on another group he had shunned and said he was open to discussions on a law that would enshrine an exemption for ultra-Orthodox Jews from mandatory military service.

Liberman and another opposition leader, Naftali Bennett, had made closing the exemption a core campaign promise and had viscerally criticised ultra-Orthodox Jews as burdens on the state, responding to wide resentment by other Israelis at a time when reservists are serving multiple tours in Gaza and Lebanon.

Eisenkot has proposed requiring national service for all Israelis, but allowing citizens to choose a civilian option rather than the military, opening the door to integrating the ultra-Orthodox.

On Friday, Eisenkot said it was urgent to replace Netanyahu, calling him a threat to the "very existence of Israeli democracy".

Following his appointment, Eisenkot will have 28 days to come up with the 61 votes needed for a government. If he comes up short, Herzog can provide a 14-day extension before he has to offer the mandate to someone else.

If neither side succeeds, Israel will head to fresh elections.

The country held five elections between 2019 and 2022 due to repeated deadlocks. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Lone gunman kills six people in Krakow, police say
articles.excerpt: Six people were killed and at least 15 wounded on Saturday when a gunman opened fire in the landmark historic…
articles.fullText:
Six people were killed and at least 15 wounded on Saturday when a gunman opened fire in the landmark historic centre of Poland's second city of Krakow, in the country's deadliest shooting in decades.

A British national was among the dead, according to police. Among the 15 wounded were nationals from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia, authorities told the PAP news agency.

The gunman, a 24-year-old Polish national who authorities said was "fascinated by far-right ideologies", was wounded by police during the rampage and is in critical condition in hospital.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced Poland would hold two days of mourning over the shooting that he called an act of "terrorism", but police did not give a possible motive.

Three more bodies were later found at the suspect's home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, around 150 kilometres northeast of Krakow. Police said they were his parents and a sister.

The suspect drove a car onto Krakow's Main Market Square and began shooting at random people, said police.

Two officers were wounded as they tried to stop the man, the police said, before shooting the suspect who was later detained and taken to a hospital.

Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was "shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting".

"My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence," he wrote on X.

An AFP reporter at the scene saw ambulances and multiple police cars as personnel cordoned off the area, one of Poland's landmark tourist hotspots popular with locals and foreign visitors.

Authorities said the man was wearing military-style clothing at the time of the attack. (AFP)

articles.title: Springboks carry out demolition of Azzurri
articles.excerpt: South Africa picked up where they left off in the Nations Championship by dismantling injury-hit Italy 66-7 in Turin on…
articles.fullText:
South Africa picked up where they left off in the Nations Championship by dismantling injury-hit Italy 66-7 in Turin on Saturday to claim a fourth consecutive bonus-point victory.

A Springboks squad boasting more than 1,000 caps ran in nine tries at the Allianz Stadium.

The victory put the world champions alone on top of the Southern Hemisphere standings with a perfect 20 points and +140 points difference following big home wins against England, Scotland and Wales in July.

South Africa face France in Paris next Friday before a trip to Ireland as they look to claim a place in the inaugural Nations Championship final at Twickenham at the end of the month.

The Azzurri will hope to bounce back in their final two home games.

They face Argentina in Genoa next Saturday before welcoming Fiji to Udine on November 21.

In Cardiff, Wales beat Japan 28-21 on Saturday to claim their second win of the inaugural Nations Championship.

Wales entertain New Zealand next weekend eyeing an unlikely first victory over the All Blacks since 1953.

Eddie Jones's Japan have just one win from four fixtures in the tournament.

Meanwhile, in Edinburgh, Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu was left lamenting his side's ill-discipline following a 43-21 defeat by New Zealand at Murrayfield.

Ewan Ashman became the first Scotland player to score a hat-trick of tries against New Zealand, the hooker's treble coming before half-time to give the hosts hope of a first win in this fixture.

The All Blacks only led 24-21 at the break but Scotland failed to score a point in a second half where Tuipulotu was sent to the sin-bin. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Arsenal extend lead as Forest topple Man City
articles.excerpt: Manchester City suffered a third consecutive Premier League defeat at the hands of Nottingham Forest on Saturday, allowing Arsenal to…
articles.fullText:
Manchester City suffered a third consecutive Premier League defeat at the hands of Nottingham Forest on Saturday, allowing Arsenal to stretch their lead at the top of the table to six points.

Enzo Maresca's men desperately needed a victory at the City Ground to keep pace with the in-form champions, who have taken 27 points from a possible 30, but lost 3-1.

City had a mountain to climb after finding themselves 2-0 down in the 18th minute following goals from defender Jair Cunha and forward Liam Delap.

The visitors were much improved after the break and Rayan Cherki cut the deficit with an emphatic strike into the roof of the net.

But Delap restored Forest's two-goal advantage in the 73rd minute, rifling home with his left foot past the outstretched hand of Gianluigi Donnarumma to earn his side breathing room.

Forest manager Oliver Glasner sprinted down the touchline to celebrate with his team, who had not managed to score a single Premier League goal at home before Saturday.

City, who won their first seven league games under new manager Maresca, know that even if they close the gap to Arsenal, it might ultimately all be in vain.

The Etihad club are still waiting to discover their fate after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules — with a huge points deduction one potential punishment.

Earlier, Arsenal made hard work of beating struggling Hull to underline their title credentials on the eve of the international break.

Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute.

Arsenal, who bossed possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy.

But VAR ruled that the German forward was in an offside position in the build-up.

Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded, but Odegaard came to Arsenal's rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher's finish.

Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled and Odegaard fired home from close range.

Arsenal manager Arteta praised his players but wants them to be more clinical after they recorded a third 1-0 win in four league games.

"We can still be much better, and we will improve in many phases, and we will get certain relationships to a different level that will be even more efficient," he said.

"That's the next step, to have bigger margins and when we have them, the opportunities, put them away to make sure that we don't have to hang in there the last few minutes."

In the early kick-off, Leeds struck in the 79th minute through substitute Noah Okafor to end Tottenham's three-match winning run.

The major talking point in the first half was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared.

Tel had to leave the field shortly before half-time.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team's second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks.

"In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn't see, I can't say nothing," he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat.

He added: "I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn't take the right decision, I don't know, but we have confidence."

Elsewhere, Jacob Murphy put Newcastle on course for a much-needed win with a spectacular strike in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage but substitute Rodrigo Muniz levelled just three minutes later to earn a 1-1 draw.

Forest's win against City means Michael Carrick's Manchester United will kick off against Aston Villa on Sunday in the relegation zone. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Substandard columns found at MTR site in Tung Chung
articles.excerpt: The Buildings Department on Saturday said it had found dozens of substandard columns at the MTR station that is currently…
articles.fullText:
The Buildings Department on Saturday said it had found dozens of substandard columns at the MTR station that is currently under construction in Tung Chung West.

Around 30 such columns were identified by the registered structural engineers (RSE) working on the project.

The department asked that the RSE submit an investigation report and propose remedial measures by the middle of this month.

The department will review these submissions, continue to monitor the situation closely, and oversee the necessary corrective works to ensure that all construction meets the relevant safety and quality standards.

In response to media questions, the department indicated that it had identified the issues during a routine site inspection and quality audit on the 27th of last month.

Upon confirming that two concrete columns were substandard, the department said it immediately instructed the RSE team and the Registered Contractor to conduct a comprehensive investigation and carry out corrective works as soon as possible.

The MTR Corporation has since ordered a suspension of relevant construction activities.

As part of standard procedures, the RSE’s supervision team carried out further inspections following the progressive removal of the concrete work, uncovering similar defects in additional concrete columns; these findings were reported to the department last Tuesday.

The department further stated that, as the temporary supports for the floor slab had not yet been removed, the identified concrete defects posed no risk to the structural integrity of the station.

These temporary supports may only be removed once a team of registered structural engineers was satisfied with the relevant works.

The department said all such procedures were carried out in accordance with the approved plans while its staff had conducted routine inspections of the site.

A preliminary review by the department revealed no evidence of intentional deviation from the approved plans, nor had it found any instances where the follow-up actions taken by the personnel in charge violated relevant codes or regulations.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Right royal row looms over Najib pardon for 1MDB sham
articles.excerpt: Malaysia's king said on Saturday that the attorney general risked denying a royal order by delaying ex-prime minister Najib Razak's…
articles.fullText:
Malaysia's king said on Saturday that the attorney general risked denying a royal order by delaying ex-prime minister Najib Razak's release from prison, adding there was no ambiguity to the pardon he was granted.

The 73-year-old Najib was jailed for his role in one of the largest-ever global plunders of a sovereign wealth fund, the now-defunct 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB).

But King Sultan Ibrahim granted him a conditional pardon in September, allowing him to serve out the rest of his sentence at home provided he pay a US$12 million fine.

On Friday, the country's attorney general blocked the former prime minister's transfer to house arrest after the fine was paid, saying his office needed more clarification on the pardon.

The king said on Saturday there was nothing to clarify, calling the pardon "clear, evident and without any ambiguity".

"There should be no confusion in interpretation," King Ibrahim said in a statement, adding it was not tied to any other cases against the former leader.

"Given that all conditions in the conditional pardon order have been fulfilled, any argument questioning the order leads towards denying the order of His Majesty the King."

Najib's lawyers thanked the monarch on Saturday, saying there was "no basis" for authorities to keep Razak in prison "a moment longer".

"They must transfer him immediately to his residence at Jalan Langgak Duta to serve his house arrest, as His Majesty has ordered," lawyer Farhan Shafee said in a statement.

The attorney general's office issued its own statement shortly afterwards, denying it was challenging the king's authority while giving no indication if it intended to immediately release Najib.

"This step is not aimed at delaying or denying the implementation of the Conditional Pardon Order, but to avoid any conflict in the implementation of the orders in force and to ensure no sentence is implemented unlawfully," it said.

A day earlier, the attorney general's office said it had sought a "temporary suspension of the execution of the house arrest" pending further investigation into the terms of Najib's pardon, adding he would remain in prison.

"During this period, his detention status shall be maintained in his existing place of detention, subject to the powers and instructions of the relevant authorities," it said.

Najib was seen leaving the Kajang Prison compound in a silver car on Friday, followed by a convoy of vehicles.

Najib did not appear at his house, and a government minister said he was just out for a previously scheduled dental appointment.

The same convoy that whisked Najib out of the prison compound returned more than four hours later under police escort.

Najib was sentenced to 12 years in prison in July 2020 in a first trial over vast sums of money siphoned from a former 1MDB subsidiary called SRC International.

But a pardons board later halved the term, and his fine was reduced to 50 million ringgit.

His sentence in this case is scheduled to be completed by August 2028.

Days after Najib's December bid for house arrest was turned down, he was sentenced to another 15 years behind bars in a separate trial, also linked to the 1MDB scandal.

Najib has also been fined 11.4 billion ringgit for his role in the corruption scandal, which took place more than a decade ago.

He is currently appealing the 15-year sentence, which is only set to start once the six-year sentence is completed. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Delhi ranked most polluted city as Diwali begins
articles.excerpt: Delhi was the world's most polluted major city on Saturday morning, according to Swiss group IQAir's live ranking, as the…
articles.fullText:
Delhi was the world's most polluted major city on Saturday morning, according to Swiss group IQAir's live ranking, as the Indian capital faced severe pollution forecasts a day before Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights.

India has ordered schools in and around Delhi to offer online classes as well as encouraged people to work from home on Sunday ahead of Diwali, which is usually marked by the widespread use of firecrackers that further worsen the air quality.

IQAir ranked Delhi first among the world's major cities at 10.35am, with a US air quality index reading of 581, double that of Lahore in neighbouring Pakistan, at 285.

IQAir's reading, based on concentrations of air pollutants, is not directly comparable to India's official index, which uses a different scale and methodology.

India's Central Pollution Control Board put Delhi's air quality index at 363 at 10am, in the "very poor" category.

Friday's air quality in Delhi was the worst pre-Diwali air in eight years, local media said, citing official data.

Pollution is an annual problem in many parts of northern India from the onset of winter as ⁠cold, heavy air traps vehicle emissions, construction dust and smoke from crop-waste burning. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: $10 meals fight social isolation
articles.excerpt: For many elderly residents and caregivers navigating the daily challenges of isolation and limited mobility, preparing a hot, nutritious meal…
articles.fullText:
For many elderly residents and caregivers navigating the daily challenges of isolation and limited mobility, preparing a hot, nutritious meal can feel like an insurmountable hurdle.

But at Shek Pai Wan Estate in Southern District, a novel community dining initiative is providing a vital lifeline, transforming a local children and youth services centre into a hub of warmth, nutrition and connection.

Run by the Aberdeen Kai-fong Welfare Association since March, the Community Dining Hall offers meals for just $10, enticing caregivers and vulnerable residents to make the trip to the centre.

“Everyone gets a good meal. That is wonderful,” said resident Leung Wah-fuk, adding that the no-MSG dishes are both delicious and healthy, which is vital for the elderly.

Fellow resident Leung Wai-chun echoed that sentiment, noting that the support is a genuine blessing for those who find it difficult to walk to the market or manage cooking alone.

Real impact
While filling daily nutritional needs is crucial, the programme’s true impact lies in its power to forge connections and spot individuals who might otherwise slip through the cracks.

Aberdeen Kai-fong Welfare Association Chief Executive Nora Ng emphasised that the target users are high-risk or hidden groups, including elderly residents living alone, caregivers, and families looking after children with special needs.

“Providing hot meals is not our main focus,” Miss Ng said. “Reaching out to high-risk or hidden groups is our main objective.”

Smart resources
This outreach-first philosophy is underpinned by smart resource allocation. Principal Assistant Secretary for Labour & Welfare (Children) Kevin Li explained that the project optimises the use of integrated children and youth services centres during their non-peak hours.

“We leverage the rich social welfare experience and manpower resources of social welfare organisations," Mr Li said.

He added that since these non-governmental organisations historically provide a wide spectrum of services - from rehabilitation to family assistance - they can quickly redeploy their resources to provide appropriate follow-up support for those identified through the dining initiative, embodying the policy goals of early identification, early intervention and sustained support.

Citywide vision
Since its launch, the pilot scheme has yielded positive results, having served more than 4,000 meals, reached nearly 400 hidden or high-risk individuals, and completed close to 350 case assessments.

Mr Li said that the programme serves as a model that effectively reduces social isolation while seamlessly catching those with hidden welfare needs.

What began as a local pilot is now blossoming into a citywide vision, newly backed by the Policy Address. Moving forward, the Government will reach out to integrated children and youth services centres across Hong Kong to invite them to join the initiative, ensuring that more isolated households feel valued, supported and truly seen.

articles.title: China icebreakers set off for Antarctica
articles.excerpt: China held a departure ceremony in Sanya, Hainan, on Saturday to mark the start of its 43rd Antarctic scientific expedition…
articles.fullText:
China held a departure ceremony in Sanya, Hainan, on Saturday to mark the start of its 43rd Antarctic scientific expedition.

Organized by the Ministry of Natural Resources, the mission will upgrade China's polar research stations and logistics network and carry out comprehensive, multidisciplinary surveys and monitoring in Antarctica.

It will also pursue priority research at the frontiers of polar science, test and apply domestically developed equipment, and deepen bilateral and multilateral cooperation in science and logistics support.

The expedition is supported by the icebreakers Xuelong and Xuelong 2, along with another vessel.

More than 600 team members from over 100 domestic institutions are participating, and the team is expected to return home in April. (Xinhua)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.fullText:

articles.title: Houthis say 33 killed in Saudi strikes in Sanaa
articles.excerpt: Houthi authorities said that Saudi strikes killed 33 people, many of them women and children, in Yemen's Sanaa province, as…
articles.fullText:
Houthi authorities said that Saudi strikes killed 33 people, many of them women and children, in Yemen's Sanaa province, as deaths mount in the country's revived civil war.

"The number of victims of the Saudi enemy warplane massacre in the Al-Shariyah area has risen... most of them children and women, while the number of wounded has risen to 30," the Houthis' Saba news agency said.

It said operations to recover victims from the rubble were ongoing and that "aircraft targeted paramedics with two strikes".

Saudi authorities have not commented on the report.

Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia said its air defences shot down a Houthi cruise missile targeting the capital Riyadh.

On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province killed 30 people. The Houthis said Saudi airstrikes were to blame, while Yemen's government forces accused the Iran-allied group of having fired a ballistic missile at the site.

Yemen slipped back into war between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government in July after years of relative calm, opening a new front in the conflict in the Middle East.

Since then, Saudi Arabia has regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has multiplied its attacks against the oil-rich kingdom. (AFP/Reuters)

articles.title: Health gear firms set to be not left to own devices
articles.excerpt: The Health Bureau said it is striving to introduce a medical devices bill next year to replace the current voluntary…
articles.fullText:
The Health Bureau said it is striving to introduce a medical devices bill next year to replace the current voluntary administrative regulatory regime.

In a paper submitted to the Legislative Council, it said a dual-track regulatory model covering both pre-market and post-market risk management would be adopted for medical devices.

This includes the implementation of a registration system and a licensing system for traders to ensure that medical devices supplied in Hong Kong meet safety and quality standards.

The paper states that the proposed registration system would primarily involve classifying different types of medical devices by risk levels.

Some general devices and in-vitro diagnostic medical devices must be registered with the Department of Health before they can be launched on the Hong Kong market.

These include hypodermic needles, vision-correction contact lenses, urine test strips and self-test blood glucose reagents.

Local manufacturers, importers and wholesalers of medical devices must obtain the relevant licences before supplying the products in Hong Kong.

The new mechanism will also require traders to report medical device-related incidents, such as incidents that pose a public health threat or may lead to death or a serious deterioration in health, and to take remedial measures that meet the department’s requirements.

The authorities stressed that the aim is to enhance regulatory oversight and mitigate the consequences of such incidents.

The legislative proposals will be discussed in a health services panel meeting on Friday.

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: France's Gehri, Russia's Isakova win HK triathlon leg
articles.excerpt: France’s Nils Serre Gehri produced a dramatic late surge to win the men’s individual title at the World Triathlon Cup…
articles.fullText:
France’s Nils Serre Gehri produced a dramatic late surge to win the men’s individual title at the World Triathlon Cup Hong Kong on Saturday, while Russia’s Diana Isakova continued her strong run of form by claiming the women’s race.

Gehri, who won the U23 title in Pontevedra, Spain, in September, clocked 50 minutes and 14 seconds.

He overtook Australia’s Callum McClusky right at the finish line to seal the victory, with Spain’s David Castro Fajardo rounding out the podium in third.

Hong Kong, China’s Nicholas Tsang finished 58th in 54 minutes and 44 seconds.

In the women’s race, Isakova arrived in Hong Kong fresh from a World Cup win in Rome and made it back-to-back victories, finishing in 55 minutes and 39 seconds.

Luxembourg’s Jeanne Lehair took second, followed by Huang Anqi of the national team.

Hilda Choi was the top finisher among Hong Kong triathletes in 37th place, with Cade Wright 39th and Bailee Brown 50th.

The roughly 24-kilometre course began along the Central and Wan Chai waterfront, with athletes opening with a 750-metre swim in Victoria Harbour.

They then tackled an 18.5-kilometre bike leg past Expo Drive, the International Finance Centre and the Central Piers before closing with a five-kilometre run to the finish line on Lung Wo Road.

The mixed team relay is scheduled for Sunday.

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Three arrested over HK$4m craft beer 'scam'
articles.excerpt: Two men and a woman have been arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to defraud in connection with an alleged scheme…
articles.fullText:
Two men and a woman have been arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to defraud in connection with an alleged scheme that induced people to invest in craft beer machines.

The suspects, aged between 46 and 54, were said to have held the roles of company director, office person-in-charge and investor recruiter, police said.

An investigation found that the syndicate began operating last November by luring people into investing in craft beer machines on the promise of high returns.

The syndicate is alleged to have claimed that the machines would be rented out on the mainland and that the annual return rate would reach 60 percent, according to police.

Officers said the syndicate held investment seminars and took prospective investors to its office to sample beer. It would initially pay returns to investors but later stopped.

Police said the syndicate had no operations in Hong Kong and that some of the invested funds were found to have been transferred to personal accounts.

So far, police have contacted six victims whose losses amounted to more than HK$4 million.

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Govt rebuts ten-nation statement on Wong case
articles.excerpt: The government on Saturday expressed strong dissatisfaction with and firm opposition to a joint statement by ten countries on the…
articles.fullText:
The government on Saturday expressed strong dissatisfaction with and firm opposition to a joint statement by ten countries on the sentencing of Joshua Wong for conspiracy to commit collusion, saying it distorted facts and smeared the SAR.

A government spokesman said the statement by the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Japan, Italy, Australia, Canada, the Netherlands and New Zealand disregarded facts, interfered with the SAR's independent judicial power, and urged the countries to stop interfering in Hong Kong matters, which are purely China's internal affairs.

Wong pleaded guilty to conspiracy to collude with foreign countries or external elements to endanger national security, and the court sentenced him independently on the evidence, the spokesperson said.

"Attempting to distort criminal judgments handed down in accordance with the law into actions targeting 'political expression' or 'political participation' is purely political manipulation deliberately intended to confuse the public and distort right and wrong," the spokesman said.

"Hong Kong is a society underpinned by the rule of law. The HKSAR Government has been consistently fulfilling its constitutional duty to safeguard national security in accordance with the law, upholding the principles that laws must be observed and strictly enforced to bring offenders to account."

Edited by Altis Wong

articles.title: Proxy votes loom large in building management law fix
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs Alice Mak said Hong Kong would strengthen provisions for proxy-vote checks and continue to…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs Alice Mak said Hong Kong would strengthen provisions for proxy-vote checks and continue to study a cap on such votes following the end of a second round of consultations on Building Management Ordinance amendments.

The public consultation drew 500 responses, with more than half expressing reservations about a proposed cap on proxy votes, Mak said on Saturday.

"If we set a cap of 20, then when proxy votes are submitted to an owners’ corporation and it receives 22, how can it determine which is the 21st or 22nd? How should the verification be carried out at submission?" she said.

"Should it be counted by the time of its submission to the management office or by the time the person signed the proxy form? So there are some practical difficulties, and we understand this."

Mak said the government would continue to study the cap and related issues, including who could be appointed as a proxy, and would explore electronic proxy appointments as a way to overcome operational difficulties.

"For the whole proxy-vote system, we must ensure, in the direction of our amendments, the system is not abused and that proxy votes cannot be forged," she said.

"We need to make sure the proxy appointment is genuine and that the operation is workable on the ground level. It has to operate practically without difficulties to avoid potential disputes."

Mak went on to say that a paper had already been submitted to the Legislative Council, and that the matter would be discussed next week.

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Lawmakers call for cancel culture to hit bid-riggers
articles.excerpt: Lawmakers on Saturday voiced hope that a newly established joint task force can change the culture of the building maintenance…
articles.fullText:
Lawmakers on Saturday voiced hope that a newly established joint task force can change the culture of the building maintenance and renovation industry by actively weeding out bad apples.

They were speaking following an announcement on Friday that 28 people had been arrested in an operation against a suspected triad-linked bid-rigging syndicate in the sector.

It was the first operation by a joint task force – made up of police, the ICAC and the Competition Commission – that was set up following the release of the report by an independent committee probing last November's deadly fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po.

Speaking on a radio programme, DAB lawmaker Chan Hok-fung said the new joint task force should not be targeting bid-rigging on a case-by-case basis.

“I think it’s only at the source that the problem can truly be solved,” he said.

“If the government doesn’t get involved, doesn’t intervene heavily and doesn’t reverse this distorted way the market operates, the problem can’t be solved."

Lam Chun-sing, who chairs the Federation of Hong Kong and Kowloon Labour Unions, called for firms convicted of bribery or competition offences to be struck off contractors' lists.

“What some contractors fear most isn’t a fine – it’s not being allowed to take on work in the future,” he said.

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: John Lee calls on youth to be curious and courageous
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee on Saturday urged young people to be curious and courageous as Hong Kong hosts the third…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee on Saturday urged young people to be curious and courageous as Hong Kong hosts the third Youth Development Summit.

In a video speech for the summit, themed "Pioneering New Horizons, Venturing into the Future", in Wan Chai, he said that when young people are empowered, communities are strengthened and the world moves forward.

Under the the territory's first five-year plan, Lee said, Hong Kong will enhance youth development opportunities, nurturing a new generation to cultivate affection for the country and Hong Kong, a global perspective, and an ambitious and positive mindset.

"We are expanding international exposure through exchanges, internships, and learning experiences," he said.

"Working with our schools, businesses and community partners, we are cultivating an environment where young people can unleash their potential, thrive and shine on the global stage."

For his part, Chief Secretary Eric Chan said he was confident government measures would help Hong Kong's young people serve the needs of the economy, the community and the country.

"That includes participating in the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, as well as the Belt and Road Initiative," he said. "We will continue to deepen patriotic education for young people while helping them broaden their international horizons."

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: He Lifeng in video talk with Bessent amid Cuba row
articles.excerpt: Vice-Premier He Lifeng, who is leading China's economic and trade affair talks with the United States, held a video call…
articles.fullText:
Vice-Premier He Lifeng, who is leading China's economic and trade affair talks with the United States, held a video call on Friday with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer.

The two sides held candid, in-depth and constructive exchanges on implementing the important consensus reached between the two heads of state at their meetings in Beijing and Washington and the outcomes of economic and trade consultations, and on key economic and trade issues of mutual concern.

The Chinese side expressed serious concern over recent US economic and trade restrictions against China.

Both sides agreed that under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, they would further leverage the China-US economic and trade consultation mechanism, continuously strengthen cooperation and properly manage differences so as to promote the stable and positive development of bilateral economic and trade relations, and contribute to building a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity.

News of the video call came as the Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday that China firmly opposes US unilateral sanctions on Chinese enterprises as the move violates international law and the basic norms of international relations.

A spokesperson for the ministry made the remarks in response to a media query that the US Department of State had announced sanctions on two Chinese enterprises and that this was reportedly the first time the United States has imposed sanctions on Chinese companies over so-called Cuba-related reasons.

In recent days, the ministry official said, the US side has escalated sanctions and suppression against China and introduced multiple discriminatory restrictions, which have seriously harmed the rights and interests of Chinese enterprises, deviated from the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, and undermined the stability of China-US economic and trade relations.

China urges the US side to correct its wrongdoings as soon as possible, the official said, noting that China reserves the right to take necessary measures to safeguard its legitimate rights and interests. (Xinhua)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: US enterprises 'surprise' in latest HK strategic batch
articles.excerpt: The United States is the largest source of overseas firms in Hong Kong’s latest batch of companies welcomed by the…
articles.fullText:
The United States is the largest source of overseas firms in Hong Kong’s latest batch of companies welcomed by the Office for Attracting Strategic Enterprises (Oases).

Last month, Oases welcomed 18 enterprise partners in its seventh batch, bringing the cumulative number of strategic enterprises attracted to Hong Kong to 142.

"In terms of overseas enterprises, you may be a bit surprised, but the United States has the largest number; of course there is also Europe," said Oases director-general Peter Yan on an RTHK radio programme on Saturday.

"This time I am also very happy that for the first time we have a Korean enterprise coming to Hong Kong and also a Japanese enterprise coming to Hong Kong as strategic enterprises."

On the mainland side, Yan said the enterprises came from various cities such as Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen.

"This time we also explored more other cities that are quite outstanding, especially in advanced manufacturing and new energy; we are also attracting them," he said.

"In medical technology, other cities are also developing quite well – for example, Hangzhou in AI, and Nanjing and Suzhou."

Yan said artificial intelligence and life and health technology are two relatively large sectors represented in the batch, with each accounting for about 30 percent of the total, while fintech and new energy each accounted for more than 10 percent.

The 142 strategic enterprises that have settled in Hong Kong, he enumerated, have committed to a total investment of HK$84 billion and will create about 26,700 high-end jobs.

His office has been monitoring and following up on the companies’ development, and both capital investment and job creation have now exceeded their targets.

Looking at the first six batches of strategic enterprises, Yan said capital investment has exceeded pledged figures by about 30 percent.

He added that Oases carefully selects strategic enterprises, gaining an in-depth understanding of about 20 to 30 percent of the companies it contacts and helping them draw up development plans for Hong Kong.

Typically, the office contacts companies several months before they settle in the city and follows up for more than a year, discussing their first concrete landing project and matching them with policies or stakeholders such as universities, investors and the business sector to help ensure a tangible industrial contribution.

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Colder weather 'may worsen flu risks for children'
articles.excerpt: A paediatric infectious diseases expert warned on Saturday that colder weather could prolong the current flu season and lead to…
articles.fullText:
A paediatric infectious diseases expert warned on Saturday that colder weather could prolong the current flu season and lead to more critical cases in children.

Mike Kwan, president of the Asian Society for Paediatric Infectious Diseases, said that if infection numbers stay high, critical cases will rise in tandem.

"Since the weather is going to get more cold, and also we are going into the winter season, I really worry that the current flu season will merge with the winter flu season," he said.

"So then you experience a very, very long period of the flu infection. And subsequently... [I am] really worried that there will be more paediatric critical cases or even mortality."

Kwan urged parents whose children had yet to receive this season's influenza vaccine to get them vaccinated as soon as possible.

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Everton in fifth heaven in comeback win over Coventry
articles.excerpt: David Moyes said Thierno Barry had proved his point after the Everton striker's double inspired a 3-1 win against Coventry…
articles.fullText:
David Moyes said Thierno Barry had proved his point after the Everton striker's double inspired a 3-1 win against Coventry on Friday.

Moyes's side trailed to Yann Gboho's goal early in the second half at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

But Barry proved too hot for Coventry to handle, netting twice in the space of just five minutes to turn the game in Everton's favour.

Barry has already reached 10 goals this season, surpassing his total for the entire 2025-26 campaign.

That miserable first season with Everton following his move from Villarreal is quickly becoming a distant memory of the in-form 24-year-old, who has six goals in his last seven appearances in all competitions.

"We gave away a really poor goal but the reaction from there was really good. Important that Thierno Barry got another couple of goals tonight which was huge for us," Moyes said.

"He can smile at me now and say I told you so and that's good. We always liked him and we want him to keep scoring."

Barry had been known for squandering chances that seemed impossible to miss last season, but he has been far more clinical this term.

"He's missed quite a few chances but tonight he got important goals for us," Moyes said after he equalled Harry Catterick's Everton record 592 games in charge.

"He's becoming an important piece for us and he's got 10 goals for us which is really good."

Among Premier League players, only Manchester City striker Erling Haaland has scored more goals than Barry in all competitions this season.

"I'm very happy because I'm a fan of him. I watch a lot of videos of him and try and do the things he does," Barry said.

"If I can stay with him until the end to get the Golden Boot I will try."

Everton are up to fifth place following their third successive win in all competitions.

"We got a performance and we got a result but I have to say Coventry made it really difficult for us. In the end we got the goals which mattered," Moyes said.

Coventry boss Frank Lampard was left frustrated with a pair of rejected penalty appeals that could have turned the match in his side's favour.

Lampard, who managed Everton from January 2022 to January 2023, said: "Big decisions affected the game, clearly.

"VAR looked at them. The James Tarkowski hair pull on Caleb Yirenkyi, then Vitaliy Mykolenko on Taiwo Awoniyi, I think he gets contact on the edge of the box which is a penalty.

"The second goal for them comes off the player's hand. If you're going to check the angles, there is an angle where it flicks in off his hand. VAR looked at it and decided not.

"The last touch to score is off the hand, in my opinion. I've seen a conclusive angle so I can disagree." (AFP)

articles.title: North Korean orphans fast tracked into state care to stem declining birth rate
articles.excerpt: Orphanages are now supplied more regularly after shift toward birth-friendly policies.
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Korean
North Korea is attempting to address its decreasing birth rate by improving the conditions of state-run orphanages while increasing crackdowns on illegal abortions, residents in the country told Radio Free Asia.
The total fertility rate for North Korea is estimated to be 1.59 children per woman of childbearing age according to key statistical indicators from South Korea’s Ministry of Data and Statistics. This is well below the replacement fertility rate of 2.1 required to maintain the population.
The rate may be even lower than estimated, a 2025 report by the Washington-based Stimson Center’s 38 North project said.
Orphanages and nurseries were previously poorly supplied, meaning that taking in more children was difficult, but government policies have improved the situation, with supplies of milk, food, clothing and shoes flowing in more regularly, the residents said.
School children arrive to pay their respects before the statues of late North Korean leaders Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il at Mansu Hill in Pyongyang on Sept. 9, 2023.
(Kim Won Jin/AFP) “Recently, authorities have been more quickly sending orphaned children or children born to unmarried women to nurseries or orphanages,” a resident of the country’s northeastern province of North Hamgyong, who requested anonymity for security reasons, told RFA. “The residents’ reaction to this is generally positive.”
The resident talked about a situation where an unmarried woman from Kyongwon county, on the border with China, had to give up her child because of the difficulty raising it alone. The child was quickly accepted into an orphanage in October.
Though the resident did not specify how long it took to place the child, another resident, from nearby South Hamgyong province, told RFA that in another case, in the coastal city of Tanchon, it took about a month.
“In September, in Tanchon, a 6-year-old child became an orphan after his mother, who had been raising him alone, died of illness,” the South Hamgyong resident said on condition of anonymity to speak freely. The child “went to an orphanage after about a month.”
Supplies meeting demand
The government’s apparent priority on supplying nurseries and orphanages has come after a series of child-friendly policies were enacted including the Childcare Law of 2022 and the Law on Preferential Treatment for Multi-Child Families of 2025. Authorities actively encourage childbirth and child-rearing, including by pushing propaganda messaging that “having many babies is patriotism.”
A woman receives the "Communist Mother's Honor Award" during the Fifth National Mothers' Convention in Pyongyang, North Korea, Dec. 4, 2023.
(KCNA via KNS/AFP) The country’s leader Kim Jong Un famously was brought to tears in 2023 when he publicly discussed the declining birth rate at the National Mothers’ Conference in December 2023.
“Putting our efforts into raising the birth rate together with mothers is a critical revolutionary undertaking that cannot be resolved by the power of our Party and government alone,” he said at the event.
Sources in RFA reports after that incident explained that women were reluctant to marry and have kids because they wanted to focus on their own happiness.
Abortion crackdown
Another way the government has been trying to prevent a declining birth rate is to punish doctors who perform abortions .
By law, abortion is illegal in North Korea, but in practice, some doctors accept payment to perform the procedure in secret.
But these days, those doctors are harder to find, the North Hamgyong resident said.
“There are women who come home pregnant after serving in the military, and they try to get rid of the baby quickly before it is seen by others,” the North Hamgyong resident said. “But recently, abortion procedures have not been easy, so many end up giving birth.”
Unwanted pregnancies happen often in North Korea because sex education is non-existent, the North Hamgyong resident said. But even if the mother gives birth, administrative hurdles and societal pressure make it very difficult to raise the child. This is because it is impossible to register the child without the father, and because of the stigma surrounding unwed mothers.
Many unwed mothers are finding creative ways to put their children born out of wedlock in orphanages without having any official record of the birth, the South Hamgyong resident said. “In late September in Tanchon, a resident found a baby wrapped in a sling in a neighborhood alley and took it to the community center.”
Students attend class in North Korea, April 2, 2018.
(KCNA via Reuters) However, it was later revealed that the person who took the child to the community center was actually the maternal uncle of the woman who had given birth, the South Hamgyong resident said. Since the fact that the unmarried woman had given birth might become a major obstacle to marriage if known to the outside world, the uncle had resorted to a workaround for his niece.
The South Hamgyong resident said that the woman did not intend to become pregnant, and had tried to get an abortion but she could not find any doctor willing to provide one.
Edited by Yi Yongin in Korean and Eugene Whong in English.
