Executive Deputy Director of the Hong Kong & Macao Work Office of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council's Hong Kong & Macao Affairs Office Xu Qifang joined the meeting.

Mr Lee remarked that Hong Kong and Shanghai have long maintained close co-operation. Since the establishment of the Hong Kong/Shanghai Co-operation Conference mechanism in 2003, he said, the two places have engaged in frequent exchanges and achieved fruitful results in areas including the economy and trade, finance, innovation and technology, education, culture and youth.

He highlighted that this year more than 400 Hong Kong enterprises took part in the ninth China International Import Expo, the highest number on record.

Mr Lee mentioned that the “Hong Kong Parallel Session”, held yesterday at the Hongqiao International Economic Forum, featured an in-depth discussion on Hong Kong's new opportunities during the 15th Five-Year Plan period, and drew Mainland enterprises’ attention to Hong Kong's unique advantage of connecting the Mainland and the world under the “one country, two systems” principle.

The Chief Executive thanked the Shanghai Municipal Government for its support, wished the expo great success, and expressed hope that the two places will continue to deepen co-operation and contribute to the country's high-quality development.

Mr Lee also remarked that Shanghai is the leading city in the Yangtze River Delta Economic City Group, while Hong Kong is one of the central cities in the Greater Bay Area, meaning both are engines driving regional economic prosperity.

The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government, he said, is now implementing Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan and pressing ahead with the development of “four centres and one hub”, which aligns closely with Shanghai's “five centres” initiative, creating further complementarity between the two cities.

Mr Lee added that Hong Kong will continue to play its roles as a “super connector” and a “super value-adder”, further the work of the Task Force on Supporting Mainland Enterprises in Going Global, and provide comprehensive support for more Mainland enterprises, including those from Shanghai, to expand into new markets.

He also thanked the Shanghai Gold Exchange for supporting Hong Kong’s development as an international gold trading centre.

The Chief Executive highlighted that the Hong Kong Precious Metals Central Clearing Company and the Shanghai Gold Exchange launched the initial phase of “Delivery Connect” this year, and that Hong Kong’s central clearing and settlement system for gold will be officially launched in the first quarter of next year.

Mr Lee concluded departed for Hong Kong in the afternoon.

articles.title: Govt condemns foreign smears
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today expressed strong dissatisfaction with and resolute opposition to various countries, led by…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today expressed strong dissatisfaction with and resolute opposition to various countries, led by the United States and other Western nations, and to anti-China media, overseas organisations, politicians and others in relation to their malicious attacks, smears and slanders following the sentence handed down by the The High Court’s Court of First Instance on Wong Chi-fung.

The court sentenced Wong Chi-fung to 10 years’ imprisonment over the offence of “conspiracy to commit collusion with foreign countries or with external elements to endanger national security”.

In a statement , the Hong Kong SAR Government emphasised that Wong Chi-fung chose to plead guilty after being given sufficient time to consider the prosecution’s evidence and having obtained legal advice, including from Senior Counsel.

It said that the entire case, including investigations, prosecution, mitigation hearings and sentencing, were conducted fairly and justly in accordance with the principles of the rule of law consistently adhered to under the common law system of Hong Kong. Wong Chi-fung also enjoys the right to appeal against his sentence in accordance with the law.

The statement highlighted that the court had stressed that the Hong Kong National Security Law (HKNSL) does not have retrospective effect and that Wong Chi-fung was not punished for his pre-HKNSL acts or activities, nor for his political ideology. It said Wong Chi-fung was convicted solely on the basis that he had persisted, after the promulgation of the HKNSL, in his conspiracy with others to commit wrongful acts endangering national security.

It added that the court found that Wong Chi-fung and absconder Law Kwun-chung adapted their roles because they were fully aware that after the HKNSL’s enactment it was unlawful to collude with foreign countries or external elements to endanger national security.

The statement said it was manifest that Wong Chi-fung knowingly breached the law, and again highlighted that he pleaded guilty to the charge and the substance of the offence, including that he conspired with absconder Law Kwun-chung and others to solicit foreign countries or external elements, including the US, to impose sanctions against, blockade or engage in other hostile activities against the People's Republic of China and the HKSAR, and their officials. This included urging the US to revoke the special treatment enjoyed by Hong Kong as a Special Administrative Region under the US law.

The Government said these acts constituted extremely serious offences which not only severely undermined national sovereignty, security, and development interests, but also directly prejudiced the well-being of the general public and the stability of society.

It added that, beyond the present case, Wong Chi-fung repeatedly broke the law, which included taking part in unlawful assemblies and contempt of court, thereby demonstrating his utter disregard for the law. The statement underlined that the punishments that he has received across all these criminal cases are fully justified, and that he has only himself to blame.

The Government reiterated that the continued smears and slanders against the HKSAR's work in safeguarding national security reflect that interference and threats from external forces still exist.

Emphasising that it will continue to uphold its constitutional duty and steadfastly safeguard national sovereignty, security, and development interests, the Government said it will continue to fulfil its duties and obligations to safeguard national security, combat and pursue anti-China and destabilising elements, as well as the agents of external forces, while simultaneously protecting the lawful rights and freedoms enjoyed by Hong Kong residents and others in the city in accordance with the law.

It urged all sides to recognise the objective facts and cease making baseless and malicious attacks and interferences.

articles.title: Overseas university heads eye NM
articles.excerpt: The World Class University Presidents Forum was held at the Hong Kong University of Science & Technology on November 4…
articles.fullText:
The World Class University Presidents Forum was held at the Hong Kong University of Science & Technology on November 4 and 5, drawing presidents and senior management from around 50 world-leading institutions.

The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is dedicated to transforming the city into an international education hub, a vision that includes developing three university towns within the Northern Metropolis (NM).

This initiative has garnered significant attention from participating universities, with university presidents from the UK, Spain and South Africa expressing interest in exploring various models of participation.

Stuart Croft, University of Warwick Vice Chancellor & President, said the Hong Kong SAR Government is being very strategic, future-oriented and globally oriented.

"With the whole concept of economic growth being driven with universities, with industry, facilitated by government, the triple helix model, where else in the world is there something of this scale and ambition?"

Professor Croft predicted that over the next decade, the world's top universities will transform their partnership model to embedding activities.

"That is what is going to make the difference, and of course the Northern Metropolis gives a fantastic opportunity for Hong Kong universities to build that embedding process, possibly earlier, possibly more deeply than elsewhere in the world, " he said.

In the latest QS Asia University Rankings, Hong Kong has five universities in Asia’s top ten.

Mosa Moshabela, Vice Chancellor & Principal of the University of Cape Town in South Africa noted that Hong Kong’s high concentration of top-tier universities, paired with its convenient transport and lifestyle, promotes student and faculty mobility while bolstering the "Study in Hong Kong" initiative.

"I think it can really offer a good place for brain circulation. For my university, for example, it would be of interest for students and faculty to come in, especially for a relatively short stay of six months. A relatively short stay would be really good for exposure, in-depth exposure to what's happening in Hong Kong, especially if it is linked to industry."

Participating presidents also highlighted the flow of talent, which they said tends to gravitate toward places with strong innovation and research ecosystems.

They expressed hope that the Hong Kong SAR Government would proactively offer incentives to attract and retain talent and support the development of the university town project.

articles.title: Bid-rigging syndicate smashed
articles.excerpt: (To watch the full press conference with sign language interpretation, click here .) The joint task force to combat bid-rigging…
articles.fullText:
(To watch the full press conference with sign language interpretation, click here .)

The joint task force to combat bid-rigging in building maintenance and renovation projects conducted a joint operation yesterday and today, successfully neutralising a bid-rigging syndicate and arresting a total of 66 people.

Led by the Security Bureau and also involving the Police Force, the Independent Commission Against Corruption, and the Competition Commission (ICAC), the two-day operation mounted by the task force was codenamed “Operation UNITEDEDGE”.

In a press conference this afternoon, Secretary for Security Tang Ping-keung gave a detailed account of it.

“During the operation, we neutralised that syndicate, resulting in the arrests of 28 people together by Police and the ICAC, including six contractors, seven directors from those contractors and six staff members of those contractors; 10 consultancy companies, involving 10 directors and two staff members; one property management company, involving one director; and one owners’ corporation, involving one member of the owners’ corporation. Some of the arrested persons have triad backgrounds.”

He continued: “The offences that they have been involved in include fraud, making a false instrument, conspiracy to defraud, conspiracy to offer advantages to an agent, and conspiracy for an agent to accept advantage.”

“The syndicate was involved with at least 20 buildings or estates, including 12 which have already awarded contracts and eight that have yet to award contracts. The awarded sum is about $100 million, and the amount to be awarded is also about $100 million.”

The investigation found that a bid-rigging syndicate with links to triad groups had attempted to “catch the last train” before reforms were implemented.

They sought to exploit fluctuations in material prices and the urgent need to commence works as pretexts to induce property owners to sign contracts before the Government introduced the “pre-qualified lists” mechanism, thereby ensuring owners selected building works consultants and contractors controlled by the syndicate.

The Security Bureau said that in the operation, the task force searched a total of 78 premises, including the offices of various contractors and consultancy firms, and the residences of those involved in the case. Documents and accounting records of the relevant building maintenance and renovation projects were also seized.

To combat triad activities, the operation also raided seven illegal premises across various districts that were controlled by the individuals with triad backgrounds. These premises included five illegal gambling establishments and two vice establishments.

Another 38 people were arrested for offences including operating a gambling establishment, gambling in a gambling establishment, and keeping a vice establishment.

Most of the arrestees remain in custody and the task force will continue with its investigations, the bureau added.

Investigations also revealed that the syndicate secured tenders through controlling the consultancy firms and contractors, manipulating the decision-making of owners' corporations (OCs) by bribing their members, and circumventing regulations by using nominal registered inspectors and works consultants.

Based on the information currently available, the bid-rigging syndicate consisted primarily of six contractors and 10 consultancy firms. It is suspected of operating the relevant companies through different individuals to conceal the connections between them, thereby gaining control over building maintenance and renovation projects.

In addition, as the consultancy firms involved also provide consultancy services on building maintenance and renovation projects for several other buildings, and the relevant works contracts have yet to be awarded, the task force will approach the relevant OCs in due course to remind them of the risks they need to be aware in awarding contracts.

The task force will also share relevant information with other government departments to support the launch of the “pre-qualified lists”, and will continue to combat bid-rigging syndicates through intelligence sharing, joint operations and prevention.

The task force has set up a 24-hour hotline, 182 000, and a reward mechanism.

Members of the public can use the hotline to provide information or intelligence regarding suspected bid-rigging activities. Personal data obtained will be kept strictly confidential.

The Government gives a stern warning that no one should flout the law by engaging in bid-rigging. Offenders will be arrested and prosecuted, and upon conviction, punished in accordance with the law.

articles.title: New child assessment unit to open
articles.excerpt: The Department of Health (DH) today announced that the Siu Sai Wan Child Assessment Centre (SWCAC) will open on December…
articles.fullText:
The Department of Health (DH) today announced that the Siu Sai Wan Child Assessment Centre (SWCAC) will open on December 21. It will replace the Ngau Tau Kok Child Assessment Centre (NKCAC), which is scheduled to close on December 19.

Located on the 7/F and 8/F of the Siu Sai Wan Health Integrated Building at 11 Harmony Road, the new centre features a floor area more than double that of the NKCAC. It is equipped with updated assessment tools and facilities to provide more comprehensive, quality services for children in need.

Arrangements will be made for children currently receiving services at the NKCAC to continue their care at either the SWCAC or another centre serving their residential districts. The DH will notify affected parents or guardians of these arrangements via SMS.

In the future, children residing on Hong Kong Island will be referred to the SWCAC. Those living in Ngau Tau Kok will be referred to the Pamela Youde Child Assessment Centre in Kwun Tong.

Additionally, the Child Assessment Service (CAS) currently provided by the DH’s seven centres will be integrated into the Hospital Authority (HA) from May 31 next year. These centres are located in Kowloon City, Kwun Tong, Kwai Chung, Sha Tin, Fanling, Tuen Mun and Siu Sai Wan.

Following the integration, the CAS will operate under the HA’s Department of Paediatrics & Adolescent Medicine at the Hong Kong Children’s Hospital. This move aims to strengthen multidisciplinary collaboration, optimise healthcare manpower, and enhance service processes and referral mechanisms.

Children suspected of having developmental or behavioural problems will receive necessary multidisciplinary assessment, treatment and rehabilitation services. They will also benefit from improved service continuity and co-ordination.

To ensure seamless care, the DH will transfer existing case information and medical records to the HA for future follow-up. The HA will send subsequent appointment notifications to parents or guardians by post or through the HA Go mobile application.

For parents or guardians who choose not to continue services under the HA, their children’s case information and medical records will not be transferred. They must contact the DH at 2246 6659 during office hours to arrange and sign the required documents, which must be returned by December 31.

The DH will dispose of and destroy those records in accordance with the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance and its internal management policies. Any appointments scheduled for or after May 31 next year will also be cancelled.

Should these children wish to consult the HA’s service at a later date, a fresh referral from a professional will be required. Appointments will then be processed in accordance with the HA’s procedures for new cases.

articles.title: FinTech Week concludes
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong FinTech Week x StartmeupHK 2026 concluded today, capping a week of discussions, business exchanges, startup showcases and ecosystem…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong FinTech Week x StartmeupHK 2026 concluded today, capping a week of discussions, business exchanges, startup showcases and ecosystem activities that brought together policymakers, regulators, entrepreneurs, investors and innovators from around the world.

The week-long programme attracted more than 48,000 visitors from over 120 economies, featured over 1,100 speakers and 800 exhibitors, and welcomed more than 30 Chinese Mainland and international delegations.

The programme was organised by the Financial Services & the Treasury Bureau, the Commerce & Economic Development Bureau and Invest Hong Kong.

Throughout the week, speakers explored how financial and technological innovation are reshaping industries, business models and global markets. Artificial intelligence (AI) discussions highlighted both the expanding potential of the technology and the foundations needed to support wider adoption.

A key highlight of the week was the finale of Global Fast Track 2026, connecting startups and scale-ups with corporate leaders, investors and potential business partners. Following over 700 applications from more than 120 economies, selected finalists presented their solutions at the main conference.

More than 30 delegations from the Chinese Mainland, including those from Beijing, Jiangsu, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Zhuhai, as well as delegations from North America, Europe, the Gulf Cooperation Council regions, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, Central Asia, and other emerging markets, participated in conference sessions, ecosystem exchanges and business engagement activities throughout the week.

Beyond the main conference, participants took part in a series of community and partner events across the city, including investor meetings, startup showcases, networking sessions and ecosystem exchanges.

During the two-day Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Immersive Executive Tour to Shenzhen, participants visited leading technology enterprises covering AI, electric vehicles, fintech and robotics, gaining first-hand insights into one of the world's most dynamic innovation ecosystems.

articles.title: Legal Week concludes
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong Legal Week 2026, themed “Collaboration & Innovation: Legal Synergy for a Shared Future” concluded today. Comprising a series…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong Legal Week 2026, themed “Collaboration & Innovation: Legal Synergy for a Shared Future” concluded today.

Comprising a series of events over five consecutive days, this year’s Legal Week demonstrated Hong Kong’s role as an international legal hub by attracting more than 6,000 registrants from over 50 jurisdictions. Participating both online and offline, they held in-depth discussions spanning various topics.

The Fourth Legal Forum on Interconnectivity & Development was held yesterday.

Supported by the Legal Affairs Department of the Liaison Office of the Central People’s Government in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the forum was co-organised by the Department of Justice and the Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the Hong Kong SAR.

Deputy Director of the Liaison Office of the Central People’s Government in the Hong Kong SAR Yuan Gujie and Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the Hong Kong SAR Cui Jianchun delivered welcome remarks.

This was followed by Counsellor of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Wang Chen and Chief Judge of the High Court Jeremy Poon delivering keynote speeches.

The forum featured two keynote sessions exploring Hong Kong’s role as an all-round international dispute resolution hub and its position in the country’s development of foreign-related rule of law.

The Second Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) Lawyers Forum, themed “Rule of Law & Legal Innovation in the GBA: Bridging Legal Talents, Fostering Synergy”, was held today, ending the week on a high note.

A leader from the Ministry of Justice, Wang Limin, delivered opening remarks and a keynote speech on the topic of supporting Hong Kong’s and Macau's legal sectors to integrate into and serve the development of China’s rule of law.

Secretary for Justice Paul Lam, Director-General of the Department of Justice of Guangdong Province Chen Xudong and Chief of Office of the Secretary for Administration & Justice of the Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region Chang Cheong all delivered opening remarks.

Mr Lam said that the GBA has unique advantages under “one country, two systems and three jurisdictions”, adding that dual-qualified GBA lawyers are pioneers who turn the differences among the three jurisdictions’ legal systems into institutional strengths.

He outlined that the GBA lawyers' scheme has been regularised from September, and that more than 700 legal practitioners from Hong Kong and Macau have obtained the relevant practising qualifications to date.

Mr Lam urged Hong Kong legal professionals to enrol in the GBA Legal Professional Examination so as to join the team of GBA lawyers as soon as possible and seize opportunities. This is also one of the objectives set out in Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan.

In a thematic sharing session, representatives from the GBA Lawyers Organization, the Law Society of Hong Kong, and the Hong Kong Bar Association exchanged insights on topics including the regularisation of the GBA lawyers' scheme, the integration of GBA legal talent and professionals, and the role of Hong Kong legal practitioners in GBA dispute resolution.

In a subsequent panel discussion, top GBA and Mainland lawyers drew on their practical experiences to explore how dual-qualified GBA lawyers can capitalise on the unique advantages of “one country, two systems and three jurisdictions” across fields such as cross-boundary commercial litigation, lawtech and green finance, to facilitate Mainland enterprises in “going global”.

The afternoon session brought together renowned Hong Kong, Mainland and Macau mediators to explore the interface of different regulatory frameworks in the GBA through the staging of a mock mediation conducted under the GBA Cross-Boundary Disputes Mediation Model Rules.

Deputy Secretary for Justice Cheung Kwok-kwan highlighted in his closing remarks that the establishment of the Task Force on Expediting the Alignment of Rules & Mechanisms in Guangdong, Hong Kong & Macao, announced in the Chief Executive’s 2026 Policy Address, will allow him to co-ordinate with relevant bureaus on ways of advancing the alignment of rules and mechanisms within the GBA. He said the task force should be established early next year.

Mr Cheung explained that the task force will draw up a list of matters relating to the alignment of rules and mechanisms, with a view to commencing relevant work with the Mainland at an early stage.

articles.title: First Bank of England rate hike in 3 years
articles.excerpt: The Bank of England raised its benchmark interest rate to 4 percent on Thursday, the first increase in more than…
articles.fullText:
The Bank of England raised its benchmark interest rate to 4 percent on Thursday, the first increase in more than three years, as soaring energy costs push up global inflation.

The central bank tightened borrowing costs by a quarter point, catching up with the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank in lifting rates since the start of the Middle East conflict.

Along with Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries, disruptions to Gulf energy supplies owing to the US-Iran war have caused record-high diesel prices around the world.

"There is now enough inflationary pressure in the pipeline caused by the rise in energy prices, that an increase in Bank Rate is warranted," BoE governor Andrew Bailey said in a statement.

"Today's increase shouldn't be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes.

"But, unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase."

Despite surging inflation, the bank upgraded its forecasts for UK economic growth in 2026 and 2027.

The central bank now estimates gross domestic product to hit 1.6 percent this year and 1.3 percent next year.

In July, it had forecast GDP output of 1.1 percent in both years.

The BoE last raised its key interest rate in August 2023, and has kept the cost of borrowing at 3.75 percent since December.

Britain's annual inflation rate accelerated by more than expected in September, rising to 3.5 percent – well above the bank's target of 2 percent.

The BoE on Thursday said its central forecast saw UK inflation peaking at 4.9 percent in the second quarter of next year.

Millions of Britons face a jump in energy bills from the start of next year, even after the government offered some assistance in its annual budget announcement last week. (AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: The Download: Texas’s fragile AI boom and energy policy shifts
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.

Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position.

Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat, Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor, and Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years. They won after making data centers a central issue on the campaign trail.

The swings could spell trouble for hyperscalers with ambitious plans in the state. They also add to growing anxiety that America’s AI buildout could stall.

Here’s how the election results could reshape AI’s future .

—James O’Donnell

What’s next for US energy policy after the midterm elections?

Democrats have taken control of both the House and the Senate, but we probably won’t see major federal climate and energy legislation while Trump remains president. The midterm elections could, however, be a big deal for energy at the state and local level.

The results could shape everything from the state grid and data center development to renewable energy and greenhouse gas emissions.

Find out what the midterms could mean for the future of US energy .

—Casey Crownhart

This story is from The Spark, our weekly climate tech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday.

A new bill could change how the US builds energy infrastructure

A sweeping bit of legislation designed to cut red tape could speed up the buildout of energy infrastructure in the US.

On November 9, the Senate is set to vote on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA). It’s a plan that could start an overhaul of the slow, complicated process for getting energy projects approved. But some environmental groups oppose the bill, or parts of it.

Explore the trade-offs behind America’s proposed permitting overhaul .

—Casey Crownhart

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 America’s data center boom has hit a political wall
Voters opposed them in 40 of 41 midterm ballot measures. ( CNBC )
+ Six cities voted to ban data centers outright. ( 404 Media )
+ Meta says building data centers has just become much harder. ( WSJ $)
+ The midterm results could also boost China’s AI ambitions. ( SCMP )
+ No one wants a data center in their backyard. ( MIT Technology Review )

2 Blood banks have become the latest victims of fridge hacks
Hackers raised the temperatures at three stores in France. ( Guardian )
+ Alarms alerted staff before any blood products were lost. ( CBS )
+ It’s an escalation after hundreds of supermarket fridge hacks. ( CNBC )
+ Experts are split over who’s behind the attacks. ( BBC )

3 Democrats are preparing to investigate Elon Musk
His firms have won over $16 billion in government contracts. ( NPR )
+ His unprecedented spending may even have hurt Republicans. ( Atlantic $)
+ Texas’s blue wave has rattled Musk and SpaceX. ( Ars Technica )

4 The new Congress could challenge Trump’s science cuts
But he can still veto any bills they pass. ( Nature )
+ Trump has already dealt many blows to science. ( MIT Technology Review )

5 China is luring AI expertise in while blocking it from leaving
It just blocked SoftBank’s bid for ABB Robotics. ( WSJ $)
+ Its chipmakers are poaching engineers from foreign rivals. ( CNBC )
+ A star mathematician has left the US to develop AI in China. ( SCMP )

6 Watchdogs have sued over tech titans advising the Pentagon
Musk and Palmer Luckey could profit from their advice. ( Military.com )

7 New research tests whether AI knows its own “thoughts”
It’s trying to map out AI’s capacity for introspection. ( Quanta )
+ AI consciousness debates are a trap. ( MIT Technology Review )

8 Astronomers are mystified by little red dots spotted by JWST
They could be the first supermassive black holes. ( Economist $)

9 Scientists have taken a first step into the zeptoverse
A rare particle decay could reveal a world smaller than atoms. ( Wired $)

10 A NASA telescope has plunged to earth after 22 years in space
Its bristles produce charges that kill bacteria. ( NBC News )

Quote of the day

“The revolt against data centers was one of the top issues of the 2026 election, and in a few years we will look back on it as just the early tremor of a much bigger AI earthquake upending American politics.”

—Greg Casar, a Democratic congressman from Texas, tells Wired that the backlash against data centers could herald a much bigger political fight over AI.

One more thing

Meet the radio-obsessed civilian shaping Ukraine’s drone defense

Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov is, at least unofficially, a spy. Once a month, he drives to the frontline in a VW van equipped with radio hardware, roof antennas, and devices that monitor drones. Over several days, he searches the skies for transmissions that can help Ukrainian troops.

Drones define this brutal conflict, and most rely on the radio communications Flash has obsessed over since childhood. Though now a civilian, the former officer has taken it upon himself to inform his country’s defense on all matters related to radio.

Unlike traditional spies, Flash shares his discoveries with over 127,000 followers—including soldiers and officials—on social media. His work has won fans in the military, but also sparked controversy among the top brass. Read the full story .

—Charlie Metcalfe

We can still have nice things

A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line .)

+ Mars has a new mystery : cliffs that look nothing like their surroundings.
+ After a long wait for clear skies, a photographer captured the perfect St Petersburg sunset .
+ Timor-Leste has eliminated trachoma , making the whole of Southeast Asia free of the blinding disease.
+ From feasting bald eagles to a northern gannet bursting through the ocean’s surface, these are the year’s best bird photos .

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo quits international football
articles.excerpt: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his intention to retire from the Portugal national team on Thursday in a social media post, bringing…
articles.fullText:
Cristiano Ronaldo announced his intention to retire from the Portugal national team on Thursday in a social media post, bringing to an end one of the most illustrious international careers in the history of football.

The 41-year-old said he would "hand back the number 7 shirt" after the November international break.

Ronaldo captained the team to their first major trophy at Euro 2016 and helped them win the 2019 and 2025 Nations Leagues.

"It was not an easy decision, because there are decisions that are not made only with the head. They are also made with the heart," said Ronaldo.

"If I ever made you happy, if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it."

Ronaldo thanked his family, the Portuguese people and the teammates, coaches and staff he worked with over his 23-year career with national team.

"Portugal will always be a part of me," he captioned the announcement video.

Ronaldo has made 234 appearances for Portugal and scored 146 goals. He holds the all-time record for international appearances and for international goals. (Reuters)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: A new bill could change how the US builds energy infrastructure
articles.excerpt: A sweeping bit of legislation designed to cut red tape could speed up the buildout of energy infrastructure in the…
articles.fullText:
A sweeping bit of legislation designed to cut red tape could speed up the buildout of energy infrastructure in the US.

With the dust barely settled on this week’s momentous midterms, the Senate is set to vote on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) on November 9. It’s a plan that could finally start an overhaul of the slow, complicated process for getting energy projects approved, as part of something called permitting reform. People on both sides of the political aisle have been pushing for this type of change for some years. 

The key question is whether this will cut greenhouse-gas emissions from the US energy sector or push them higher still.

The federal permitting system is designed to protect the environment against industrial pollution from large projects like power plants, transmission lines, and natural-gas pipelines. Today, permitting is governed by a range of laws, including the National Environmental Policy Act and the Clean Water Act. And if there’s one thing you might know about the current state of permitting in the US it’s that it’s slow and incredibly complicated.

So in its 417 pages, BAAJA attempts to tighten things up. The bill has provisions that narrow the sorts of projects that need to apply for federal permits and others that enact deadlines in hopes of speeding up a process that today can take years. (There are also specific provisions about transmission planning, mining, and the rest of the kitchen sink; this thing is dense .)

One thing to know about this bill is that it’s largely technology neutral: It opens the doors for the buildout of projects involving both fossil fuels and renewables. So there’s a weird mishmash of legislators and outside groups supporting it.

The bill’s four sponsors in the Senate are two Republicans and two Democrats. The White House has backed this permitting reform bill, with its Council of Economic Advisors finding that it would reduce review times and have economic benefits like boosting GDP.

Clean energy groups like the American Clean Power Association have largely come out in favor of the bill too, with the group’s analysis finding that it could unlock 350 gigawatts of new clean energy for the grid.

Some environmental groups, however, oppose the bill, or parts of it. An assessment from the Natural Resources Defense Council says the parts about transmission could have substantial benefits for the grid, but the narrowing of environmental reviews could be damaging for public and private lands.

Many in the climate world have long been calling for permitting reform, arguing that renewables stand to benefit more than fossil fuels. The thinking is that solar and wind power are some of the cheapest sources available today, so if we unlock the ability to build more energy, they are likely to win out economically.

A few early analyses have tried to quantify just what BAAJA would mean for emissions in the US. One, from the think tank Rhodium Group, found that in the best-case scenario, the bill would cut economy-wide emissions by 4%, reduce annual energy bills by $78 per household, and add 200 gigawatts of new clean energy by 2040. In the worst case, emissions would stay about the same.

Another report , from the nonprofit research group Resources for the Future, found that the bill could cut power-sector emissions 6% by 2041 and save more than $350 billion on system costs by midcentury.

But there are some concerns that this permitting bill’s real effect would be to open the floodgates for new natural-gas plants. As data centers have put more pressure on the grid, a wave of such plants have been announced.

“You get down to a trade-off between essentially growing the clean electricity industry on the one hand and then, as a compromise, growing the fossil-fuel industry on the other,” says Kevin Kircher, an energy modeler and assistant professor of mechanical engineering at Purdue.

To quantify that trade-off, Kircher also modeled the potential emissions effects of the bill and found that if BAAJA had been in place in 2025, energy sector emissions would have been higher than the actual baseline. Health and mortality risks associated with air pollution would also have increased.

This bill is scheduled for a Senate vote on November 9, well before the next Congress takes control. It’s not clear what the dramatic victories for Democrats might mean for the legislation, which was expected to pass the Senate with largely Republican support if a few Democrats got on board. Democrats could decide to wait for next year, when they’ll have control of both chambers. But any deal would ultimately need to win Trump’s signature, limiting what a future bill might be able to change.

In a world where permitting new projects is easier, we’ll see more clean energy, but we’ll see more natural gas, too. And while prices could get lower, that could push demand for electricity higher, leading to more emissions overall.

Simplifying the permitting system and cutting red tape is a worthy goal. But when it comes to emissions, it still really matters what, exactly, you want to build.

articles.title: Kane 'feels right at home' with Bayern extension
articles.excerpt: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane has signed a contract extension with Bayern Munich until June 30, 2029, the Bundesliga club…
articles.fullText:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane has signed a contract extension with Bayern Munich until June 30, 2029, the Bundesliga club said on Thursday.

The England captain joined Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023 and has since helped the German side win two Bundesliga titles, the German Cup and two German Super Cups.

The 33-year-old striker has scored 156 goals in 161 appearances in all competitions for Bayern and capped his prolific spell in Munich by winning the Ballon d'Or last week.

He was the first Englishman to win the prestigious award since Michael Owen in 2001.

"I feel right at home at FC Bayern," Kane said in a statement.

"I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich. We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager.

"It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I'm now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club."

Kane has frequently been linked with a move back to England, where he remains 47 goals shy of Alan Shearer's Premier League record of 260 goals.

However, the striker said in August that the Premier League no longer holds the same appeal for him as he is focused on his career in Germany.

"Since joining us in 2023, he has achieved extraordinary things with his goals, his influence on the game and as a role model both on and off the pitch," Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen said.

"His contract extension is a commitment to FC Bayern and to a story that is far from over."

Bayern did not disclose financial details of the agreement. However, German media reported that the extension is the most lucrative contract in the club's history and part of a long-term commitment to the England captain.

Kane has finished as the Bundesliga's top scorer in each of his seasons with Bayern and was named Germany's Footballer of the Year in 2026.

He has also won the European Golden Shoe twice, awarded to Europe's leading league goalscorer, and captained England to a third-place finish at this year's World Cup. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK cheer as Trump thumping may spell woe for AI boom
articles.excerpt: Tech firms tumbled Thursday as investors contemplated the outlook for the AI boom after Democrats swept the US midterms, partly…
articles.fullText:
Tech firms tumbled Thursday as investors contemplated the outlook for the AI boom after Democrats swept the US midterms, partly on the back of growing anger over the rapid building of data centres across the country.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index soared 877 points, or 3.7 percent, to end at 24,796 on comparatively high turnover of HK$356.67 billion.

The tech index rose 218 points, or 5.5 percent, to 4,154 while the China enterprises index gained 311 points, or 3.9 percent, to 8,369.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index closed up three points, or 0.1 percent, at 3,689 on turnover of 979.71 billion yuan.

The Shenzhen Component Index was 135 points, or 1.2 percent, higher at 11,471 on turnover of nearly 1.14 trillion yuan while the ChiNext Index was up 22 points, or 0.87 percent at 2,566 on turnover of 576.11 billion yuan.

The tech losses, which happened mostly in tech-heavy benchmarks like the Nikkei and Kospi, came after US President Donald Trump's Republicans were dealt an historic defeat that was blamed on high prices, tariffs and the Iran war.

The result stoked hopes he will look to wind down the Middle East conflict, which would help temper inflation and even soften his stance on trade.

But AI-linked firms came under the cosh amid fears for planned data centre construction projects as well as renewed scrutiny from newly installed Democrats on Capitol Hill.

The sector had already been in the crosshairs of investors owing to questions about the vast sums pumped into new facilities, R&D and chip development, and when any companies would see a profit.

Charu Chanana at Saxo Markets said the vote was accelerating a reassessment of AI that was already under way.

"A Democratic Congress introduces another layer of uncertainty: regulatory scrutiny," she wrote, adding that the three main risks were more oversight, data centre restrictions and capital spending uncertainty.

"The congressional scrutiny could accelerate demands for AI safety standards, independent model evaluations and greater accountability for data centre developers."

However, Chanana also said: "This is not the same as an outright anti-AI policy agenda. AI is strategically important for US competitiveness, particularly against China, and there remains considerable bipartisan interest in maintaining American leadership."

In Tokyo, the Nikkei ended 1,110 points, or 1.79 percent, in the red at 61,077, dragged lower by a sharp selloff in AI and chip shares even as the vast majority of stocks on the index rose.

The broader Topix index gained 45 points, or 1.2 percent, to 3,940.

In Seoul, the Kospi closed down 300 points, or 5.28 percent, at 5,383 to a seven-month closing low, as chipmakers tracked overnight losses in US tech stocks on worries about a slowdown in AI investment following a Democratic win in the midterm elections. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK 'to widen trade reach to help nation go global'
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee on Thursday said Hong Kong would continue to expand its international trade network to better contribute…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee on Thursday said Hong Kong would continue to expand its international trade network to better contribute to the country's overall development.

Speaking at the Hong Kong sub-forum of the Hongqiao International Economic Forum in Shanghai, he noted the event was the first major conference held by the SAR since the unveiling of its first-ever five-year plan in September.

The conference, Lee said, allowed experts and industry leaders from both the mainland and Hong Kong to gather and explore how the city could leverage its unique position under "One Country, Two Systems" and integrate into national development.

One key focus area is trade, he said.

“Hong Kong has become the fifth-largest merchandise trading entity in the world, having signed free-trade agreements with 21 economies and investment agreements with 34 economies," Lee said.

"The SAR government will continue to expand its international economic and trade network to play a greater role in the country’s high-standard opening up."

The world, Lee pointed out, is experiencing a once-in-a-century transformation, which is happening alongside a global supply chain restructuring and rapid technological advancement.

He stressed that Hong Kong must proactively plan for its future and implement a forward-looking strategic plan with a calm and measured approach.

Another key focus area, Lee said, is finance.

Describing it as Hong Kong’s fundamental and greatest area of strength, he stressed that the SAR must consolidate its role as an international financial centre.

He added that Hong Kong would strengthen its position as the world's largest offshore renminbi hub to expand the global use of the currency and actively build a commodity and gold trading ecosystem.

Lee also noted that Hong Kong would proactively align with national scientific research and industrial strategies, accelerate its investment in science and technology, and help mainland enterprises expand overseas through its GoGlobal Task Force.

Later, Lee toured various booths hosted by Hong Kong enterprises and institutions taking part in the China International Import Expo, which is being held concurrently with the forum.

He listened to a briefing by Hong Kong Polytechnic University representatives, and at one booth, tasted traditional sweetheart cakes — also known as wife cakes.

A representative told the chief executive that the pastries have been a huge hit at high-speed rail stations on the mainland, adding that they have revamped their packaging to feature Hong Kong elements on the design, such as trams, to appeal to younger generations.

Lee also visited a craft beer booth to try a brew infused with the flavour of salty-lemon 7Up — an iconic Hong Kong cha chaan teng drink that mixes 7Up with salted preserved lemon.

A representative at the booth told him that Hong Kong enjoys a major advantage in sourcing raw ingredients thanks to being a highly international city.

Lee said Hong Kong could host its own beer festival in the future, encouraging the business to keep growing and build itself into a premier local brand for such events.

Frederick Ma, chairman of the Hong Kong Trade Development Council, said the council led a delegation of more than 70 Hong Kong enterprises at this year's expo, with records set in both the number of participating exhibitors and the amount of exhibition space used.

_____________________________
Last updated: 2026-11-05 HKT 17:10

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Top import expo opens in Shanghai
articles.excerpt: The ninth edition of the China International Import Expo opened in Shanghai on Thursday amid fanfare. It's the country's largest…
articles.fullText:
The ninth edition of the China International Import Expo opened in Shanghai on Thursday amid fanfare.

It's the country's largest import expo and the world's first national-level exhibition dedicated to imports.

Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang delivered a keynote speech at the opening ceremony.

"China's continuous hosting of the China International Import Expo is not only a concrete measure to proactively expand imports, but more importantly, a practical action to advocate for an open world economy, promote a proactive, dynamic and upward trade balance, and drive global development towards becoming more balanced, coordinated and inclusive," he said.

“Everyone is concerned about trade market issues, the key is how to realise trade balance.”

This year's event, which runs through November 10, has attracted 4,142 overseas exhibitors from more than 160 countries, regions and international organisations.

More than 480 exhibits are making their global, Asian or China debuts at the 2026 event, the highest number ever.

This year's expo retains its six major exhibition areas and an innovation incubation section, covering areas such as intelligent industry and information technology, consumer goods, food and agricultural products, automobiles and smart mobility, medical devices and healthcare products, and trade in services. (Xinhua and agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK 'is largest cross-boundary wealth management hub'
articles.excerpt: Financial Secretary Paul Chan on Thursday said Hong Kong’s wealth management sector is growing strongly and is well positioned to…
articles.fullText:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan on Thursday said Hong Kong’s wealth management sector is growing strongly and is well positioned to capture a fair share of business emanating from shifting global affluence.

In a keynote speech at the Wealth Management Summit, he pointed to a survey in July by the Securities and Futures Commission that showed assets under management jumped 20 percent to more than HK$42 trillion.

The city, Chan said, is now the largest cross-boundary wealth management centre in the world.

A survey by summit organiser Private Wealth Management Association offered a similarly encouraging picture, as it found 77 percent of member firms reported stronger demand to open accounts or book client assets in Hong Kong and that 94 percent were moderately or highly optimistic about the city's prospects over the next five years.

Chan said sentiment at this week’s Global Financial Leaders’ Investment Summit, which drew some 280 international leaders from the sector, including around 120 chairmen or chief executives, was "decidedly positive", with some planning to increase investment and headcount in the city.

International capital was showing fresh confidence in Hong Kong, he said, with it being reinforced by policy measures to boost private wealth management.

"Our tax concession for family-owned investment vehicles is now well established and Hong Kong is home to over 3,300 single-family offices, up 25 percent in just two years," he said at the summit.

"The New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme has received some 4,300 applications, representing an expected investment of HK$150 billion, and we have introduced legislation to further enhance the preferential tax regimes for funds, single-family offices and carry interest, which we aim to pass by the end of this year."

Chan said higher rates and uncertainty were redrawing the map for capital flows, with cash earning a return again and investors diversifying across markets and currencies.

Hong Kong is a clear beneficiary, he said, noting that deposits rose 7.7 percent to HK$20.9 trillion in the first nine months of this year.

Initial public offerings raised, Chan pointed out, a record HK$388 billion and capital is arriving from the United States and Europe, as well as the mainland, Southeast Asia, Central Asia and the Middle East.

He also pointed to technology and AI as a growing source of wealth: tech is now the largest source of wealth among the world's richest tycoons, and mainland billionaire fortunes rose over 20 percent to US$1.8 trillion last year.

Hong Kong is capturing it at source – 116 A- and H-share listings in the first three quarters accounted for about 70 percent of funds raised, over half of which were in AI, semiconductors and robotics, with some 500 applications in the pipeline.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK stocks gallop up as midterms fuel caution in region
articles.excerpt: Oil, chip stocks and the US dollar were under pressure in Asia on Thursday and just about everything else was…
articles.fullText:
Oil, chip stocks and the US dollar were under pressure in Asia on Thursday and just about everything else was up after US voters swept the Democrats to a series of stunning midterm election wins, a result that raised hopes for an end to the country's war on Iran.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened up 397 points, or 1.66 percent, at 24,316 and almost doubled its gains to be 784 points up in early trading.

The tech index rose 56 points, or 1.43 percent, to open at 3,992 while the China enterprises index too was higher by a similar margin, putting on 116 points, or 1.45 percent, to 8,174.

Up north, the Shanghai Composite Index opened down 39 points, or 1.1 percent, at 3,646.

That downward trend held too for the Shenzhen Component Index, putting it 118 points, or 1.1 percent, lower at 11,216 while the ChiNext Index was 51 points, or two percent, down at 2,493.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 196 points, or 0.32 percent, higher at 62,384, buoyed by declines in crude oil but with gains held in check by fears that the US midterms trashing for President Donald Trump will result in Democrats slowing the pace of AI data centre expansion.

The 225 benchmark was 104 points down at one stage before noon.

In Seoul, the Kospi opened 103 points, or 1.82 percent, lower at 5,580 on fears for AI and chip shares and was 182 points down at one stage before lunch.

Brent crude futures dived nearly 9 percent overnight, falling below US$100 a barrel.

Brent has dropped by about 20 percent so far this week.

If sustained through to Friday's close, it would make for the largest weekly drop in oil prices since a week in April 2020 when US crude briefly fell into negative territory.

Tumbling energy prices encouraged a rally in bonds, which lowered yields, pulled the dollar to a one-month low of US$1.1273 per euro, and helped stocks.

Solar supply chain stocks jumped the most, in anticipation of Democrats boosting support for renewables, while shares in data centre companies and their equipment suppliers across Asia fell on expectations of tougher regulation.

Democratic data-centre opponents who campaigned, in part, on moratoriums on the AI linchpin won stunning victories in Texas and Georgia in a sign public opinion is shifting on the booming sector.

To be sure, most analysts think it ultimately won't dent demand for artificial intelligence, data centres or computer chips but do now expect at least a temporary slowdown.

"The magnitude of the victory is what has caught markets off guard," said Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne.

At US$93.50, oil was testing overnight lows in the Asia morning as traders chose to bet that Trump, facing a Democratic Congress and hurt by high energy prices caused by the Mideast conflict, would be less likely to escalate the war with Iran.

Trump acknowledged on Wednesday that the war played a role in Republicans' defeat and his vice president, JD Vance, was even more blunt on X: "The reason we lost is the war."

A resolution could push oil prices lower still, alleviating inflation pressure and reducing the likelihood of future interest rate hikes. (Reuters/Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Djokovic to miss ATP Finals after early Paris exit
articles.excerpt: Novak Djokovic crashed out of the Paris Masters on Wednesday after the 24-time Grand Slam champion lost 2-6, 6-3, 6-3…
articles.fullText:
Novak Djokovic crashed out of the Paris Masters on Wednesday after the 24-time Grand Slam champion lost 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 to Australian qualifier Rinky Hijikata in the second round.

The shock defeat by the world number 83 ended the 39-year-old Serb's hopes of qualifying for the ATP Finals later this month.

Speaking in the mixed zone after the loss, Djokovic told reporters his plan for the next few weeks was "just rest".

"I'm looking forward to it," the 39-year-old added.

After sailing through the first set, Djokovic soon found himself in a battle with the Australian qualifier.

Hijikata broke Djokovic in the eighth game of the second frame before serving out to force a decider.

The third set ground on until the Serb cracked serving at 3-3 to hand his unfancied opponent a chance at victory, which he duly took with a second break to seal the match in style.

Djokovic, a seven-time champion in Paris, said he felt "disappointment obviously, losing a match that I felt like I was dominating for the first set".

But he heaped praise on Hijikata for the way he responded.

"He was switched on, I wasn't serving as well and he was just playing out of his mind honestly. He was not missing and keeping the ball low and just a terrific performance," Djokovic said. (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: Zverev loses first match as World No. 1 in Paris
articles.excerpt: Alexander Zverev made a losing start to his reign as world number one on Wednesday as the two-time Grand Slam…
articles.fullText:
Alexander Zverev made a losing start to his reign as world number one on Wednesday as the two-time Grand Slam champion went down 7-6 (7/5), 6-2 to an inspired Lorenzo Musetti at the Paris Masters.

Playing his opening match in the round of 32 in the French capital, the German accumulated errors to tamely exit the tournament against the 24-year-old Italian.

Former World No. 5 Musetti became the fifth man to defeat a player in his opening match as the world number one.

But Zverev insisted that the pressure of being the top-ranked player was not the cause of his poor performance.

"Stress, I don't know if stress. I was a bit annoyed, to be honest," he told reporters.

"The last couple of days, because, you know, achieving the World No. 1 status is something that I think every player dreams of.

"But then I feel like I'm the only World No. 1 in tennis history that has to explain why it's okay for me to be World No. 1, which I find quite difficult, because I think I deserve to be where I am, even though I lost today."

In the opening set, both players staved off break points in consecutive games midway through the frame, but it always looked destined to be decided by a tie-break.

The Hamburg native got ahead 5-2 in the breaker but Musetti rallied to string together a run of five consecutive points to take a one-set lead, sealing it with a huge serve out wide to Zverev's backhand.

The Italian was now brimming with confidence and after failing to convert a break opportunity in the first game of the second set, he made no mistake two games later as he capitalised on an error-strewn display from Zverev.

Musetti continued to deploy a sliced backhand to devastating effect as unforced errors mounted on the 2024 Paris Masters champion's side of the net, culminating in a second break which allowed the Italian to serve for the match.

The world number 24 did just that, sealing his progress to the last 16 to love against a dejected Zverev.

"Personally, I felt that today, I was enjoying (it), even when I was losing in the tie-break, I kept that in mind to enjoy, you know, the beauty of this sport," Musetti said on-court.

"It paid off, I'm really, really happy."

Zverev, himself, recognised that the Tuscan was a level above him on the day.

"To simplify it, he played really good and I played really bad," the 29-year-old said.

"I think this was not a very good match from me, I think it might be one of the worst in the last couple of months." (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: Real stay perfect in Champions League as City hold on
articles.excerpt: Federico Valverde lashed home a stunning effort from distance to snatch Real Madrid a late 3-2 victory at AEK Athens…
articles.fullText:
Federico Valverde lashed home a stunning effort from distance to snatch Real Madrid a late 3-2 victory at AEK Athens on Wednesday in the Champions League and preserve their 100 percent start.

Jose Mourinho's side twice came from behind against the Greek champions before Valverde claimed all three points for his side, level with holders Paris Saint-Germain on four wins from four league phase games.

Aboubakary Koita sent AEK ahead after 12 minutes and Jude Bellingham equalised with a sublime flick for the record 15-time winners.

Stavros Pilios sent the Greek champions ahead with 15 minutes to go but Kylian Mbappe swiftly pulled Madrid level once again, setting the stage for Valverde's late winner.

Madrid have now won seven straight games across all competitions.

Meanwhile, Erling Haaland's 78th-minute strike helped Manchester City shake off a mini-slump with a 3-2 win at RB Leipzig.

After an excellent start to the season, City had lost two Premier League games in a row either side of beating Brighton on penalties in the League Cup.

The visitors twice went ahead through a Castello Lukeba own goal and an Enzo Fernandez header, only to be pegged back by goals from Ridle Baku and Antonio Nusa.

Despite having scored more against Leipzig than any other opponents in his career, Haaland had few chances but was right on the spot to turn in an Elliot Anderson cross for the winner.

"For me I think it's easy. It's around 100 minutes a game to just stay fully focused," Haaland told reporters.

"In this period it was about trying to wait for the right moment and attack it in the right way and put it in the back of the net and that's exactly what I did."

Haaland has now scored 13 times in nine matches against Leipzig, including a memorable five-goal performance in a 7-0 rout in March 2023.

Despite the victory, City were well below their usual best against a Leipzig side in a rebuilding process under new coach Martin Demichelis.

City coach Enzo Maresca, who arrived in the summer, conceded his side were still a "work in progress" but praised Haaland.

"It's important that he's on his game. We know that at any moment he can help us, he can score goals," Maresca said.

Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres scored in the first half to hand Arsenal a 2-1 win at Slavia Prague.

Arsenal got back to winning ways in Europe after a 2-2 draw at Bayern last month, reaching 10 points from four Champions League games so far, while Slavia have a single point in the standings.

Liverpool's perfect record in this season's Champions League ended in a 3-2 loss to Fenerbahce in Turkiye, while Como hit nine away to Lens in an incredible performance as they equalled the biggest winning margin in the competition's history (AFP).

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Stocks surge, oil tumbles after Trump's election rout
articles.excerpt: Wall Street stocks surged on Wednesday as markets greeted the resolution of US midterm elections while oil prices tumbled on…
articles.fullText:
Wall Street stocks surged on Wednesday as markets greeted the resolution of US midterm elections while oil prices tumbled on expectations the Democratic sweep could hasten a resolution to the US-Iran war.

Democrats seized control of both houses of Congress in a victory that gives them the power to block legislation, open investigations into Trump's administration and influence government budgets, including the Pentagon.

Heading into Tuesday's vote, some investors had viewed a decisive Democratic win as representing trouble for stocks, citing the risk to the buildout of artificial intelligence data centres.

But stocks bounced on Wednesday as analysts said the election outcome resolved uncertainty and pointed to relief that Trump did not contest the results.

Oil prices were under pressure throughout the session, adding to losses after US Vice President JD Vance said in a social media post that the Republican defeat was due to the unpopularity of the Iran war, which has sent the prices of fuel and other staples soaring.

Crude prices finished the day down more than eight percent with both major contracts under US$100 a barrel.

"I think that the election might be leading the market to conclude that Trump might now be inclined to make a deal," said Andy Lipow of Lipow Oil Associates. "Also, with the Democrats in charge of the Senate and House, they may be inclined to restrict funding for the war, and that forces Trump into ending the conflict."

The drop in oil prices added momentum to Wall Street stocks, which opened higher following positive sessions on leading European exchanges.

All three major indices finished solidly higher, with the Dow ending up three percent, or more than 1,500 points at 53,356.

Opposition to data centres fuelled campaigns in key states like Texas, Georgia and Ohio where Democrats won gubernatorial elections previously held by Republicans.

But Wednesday's gains by Microsoft, Amazon and other hyperscalers suggest markets may see an upside to constraints that deter overbuilding, said Steve Sosnick of Interactive Brokers.

"At some level, people are happy that the industry might be saved from its own worst instincts," said Sosnick, who noted that Nvidia and other chipmakers fell following the results.

Both of Elon Musk's publicly traded companies fell after the billionaire's huge political donations failed to stop the Democratic tide. SpaceX fell 3.8 percent and Tesla dropped 3.3 percent.

Lockheed Martin, which lost 6.9 percent, was among the defence companies that retreated, while First Solar jumped 4.6 as the election lifted the prospects for renewable energy.

Earlier, Europe's main indices finished with gains of around two percent despite official data on Wednesday showing that eurozone inflation reached a three-year high of 4.0 percent in October.

Markets across Asia also performed strongly, though Tokyo ended lower as its tech sector struggled.

The S&P 500 rose 1.6 percent, to 7,689, the Dow rose 3 percent, to 53,356, while the Nasdaq rose 1.4 percent, to 25,737. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
articles.excerpt: Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI buildouts. But…
articles.fullText:
Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position.

Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat against Ken Paxton. Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor against the Republican incumbent, Greg Abbott. At the state level, Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years. Talarico and Hinojosa made data centers a central issue, discussing them constantly on the campaign trail.

Even before the polls closed, insiders in the data center industry noticed that the times were changing. At the industry’s DCD conference in Ashburn, Virginia, on Tuesday, panelists lamented that Texas had been the easiest place to build for years—until September. That’s when Abbott, perhaps seeing the increasingly bipartisan distaste for these facilities , began changing course himself.

Developers said the governor’s office had stopped responding to their emails. On September 21, Abbott directed a key state regulator to halt data center permits. Many panelists at the conference were expecting this to mean that existing projects might be slowed and new ones could be halted altogether.

The governor-elect indeed seems eager to do that. Hinojosa supported tax breaks for data centers in 2023 as a way to boost construction jobs, but during her campaign she began pushing for a full-fledged moratorium.

That would be a problem for the hyperscalers of Big Tech, which have ambitious plans for AI training facilities in the state. The scale of projects already underway in Texas is massive. The Stargate Frontier data center in Shackelford County is projected to serve 1,820 megawatts—about as much as the nation’s largest data center, SpaceX’s Colossus 2 in Tennessee, and more than twice as much as the largest data center currently operating in Texas. Nexus Hubbard, also under construction and intended mostly to serve Anthropic, has a planned size of 6,400 megawatts and is the second-largest data center being built in the US, behind only Meta’s Hyperion project in Louisiana.

The potential for Democrats to order delays to these projects or moratoriums on new ones adds to growing anxiety that the AI buildout could stall. Banks and lenders are already getting pickier about the projects they back. And given the extent to which the data center buildout is underpinning growth in the economy right now, those forces combined could have ripple effects.

Voters around the country, though, were unambiguous in the midterms, sending a similar message on everything from state ballot questions to national offices. Voters supported efforts to protect ratepayers from increases in their electricity bills caused by data centers, and they favored some larger bans on new data centers altogether. If we needed any more convincing that Big Tech has fumbled its effort to sell voters on the idea that AI-powered abundance will make health care better, goods cheaper, and scientific breakthroughs more common, this was it.

A key question is whether the Texas counties with the largest data center presence were part of the reason these Democrats got elected, or if the anti-data-center vote came from elsewhere.

It’s complicated: The counties where much of the data center buildout is happening are around Dallas. Dallas County and others closest to it predictably went blue, but nearby Ellis County, which leads in permitting requests for data centers, went for Greg Abbott and Ken Paxton. Cameron County, near the state’s southern border, is a hot spot for data centers and voted blue in the midterms, which was a shift. But Mitchell County and Scurry County, where a bunch of projects in west Texas are located, went red.

This is a big deal, because no single office in the state decides whether a project goes ahead or is halted. Decisions often reflect an interplay between city governments, county officials, and state offices.

Local officials who have some say over data center development may resist sweeping restrictions from the state. And Democrats pushing for a moratorium might also face pushback from the construction unions that supported some of their campaigns. So while the blue wave spells a death knell for Texas data centers in theory, election winners may find that following through on their opposition once in office is much more complicated than campaigning on it.
