articles.title: What’s next for US energy policy after the midterm elections?
articles.excerpt: I’ve been locked in to my various screens since results from midterm elections started to roll in last night. And…
articles.fullText:
I’ve been locked in to my various screens since results from midterm elections started to roll in last night. And it didn’t take long to see the beginning of the blue wave: Democrats took control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate, a dramatic swing from Donald Trump’s victory two years ago.

While the results are striking, we probably won’t be seeing some of the big climate and energy policy shifts that have come in recent years as Congress and the presidency have changed hands. Instead, we’re entering a period of divided government, with a Congress that will likely do battle with Trump’s White House over the next two years. But even if the federal government isn’t likely to pass laws that overhaul energy and climate policy, the midterm results could be a big deal for energy, especially at the state and local level.

Let’s step back for just a moment to put these results in context. Readers might remember huge laws affecting climate and energy that were passed in just the last four years. The 2022 Inflation Reduction Act included massive support for clean energy, including tax credits and government grants and loans. Then the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act essentially slashed much of the support and financial incentives in the IRA from two years before.

What those two laws had in common was a period when the government was entirely united, with the Senate, House of Representatives, and presidency all controlled by the same party—the Democrats in the first case and the Republicans in the second.

Now Democrats have captured a majority in both the Senate and the House. But Donald Trump is still in the White House. And crucially, neither chamber is anywhere close to a two-thirds Democratic majority. That’s the ratio that would be needed to override a presidential veto.

So even if Congress puts together new legislation to boost climate measures and clean energy, Trump will need to sign it—and that dramatically narrows the scope of what might happen legislatively between now and the next election.

There could be some bipartisan compromises. One interesting bit of legislation to watch immediately after the election is what happens with permitting reform. In late September, a bipartisan group of senators put forward a bill that would overhaul how new energy projects are reviewed and approved in the US. The law aims to cut red tape and speed up the permitting process.

The Senate is set to vote on that package, called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, on November 9, before the new Congress takes control in January. The White House has supported the bill, and it could pass the Senate if just a handful of Democrats join the Republican majority. But now, we might see Democrats wait until next year to try to renegotiate a deal, though anything would still need to pass muster with Trump.

With Democratic control of Congress, we’ll likely see much more scrutiny of Trump and agencies controlled by his appointees. Democratic leaders have already signaled plans to go after leaders like EPA commissioner Lee Zeldin over cuts to staff and investments. Democrats will have the power to subpoena cabinet members and open investigations.

Looking beyond the national results, a major trend to watch moving forward will be local action. Democrats swept local control of Pennsylvania, and officials there have signaled plans to support renewable energy and efforts to cut greenhouse-gas emissions. Democrats also took control of the Georgia Public Service Commission for the first time in 30 years. The group regulates electric utilities, essentially controlling much of the grid’s buildout.

Among the broadest effects of these election results, though, will be for the data center industry. According to tracking from Ballotpedia, there were 41 local ballot questions related to data centers. And overwhelmingly, voters chose to restrict their development. Nearly every single one of these measures looks set to come down against data center development, as of the morning of November 4.

And AI critics fared well in their races, too. Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the governor’s seat in Texas, ousting Republican incumbent Greg Abbott. During her campaign, Hinojosa called for a law to completely pause data center development; if passed, it could have major implications for both the state’s grid and the data center industry more broadly.

We might not see dramatic new climate- or energy-related federal legislation between now and the next major US election. But many voters signaled, and quite loudly, that they wanted a change. We’ll see how much will shift in the next two years, and where that leaves us.

This article is from The Spark, MIT Technology Review ’s weekly climate newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Wednesday, sign up here .

articles.title: Govt rejects remarks on sentencing
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today expressed strong opposition to remarks made by the spokesperson of the US…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today expressed strong opposition to remarks made by the spokesperson of the US Consulate General in Hong Kong concerning the sentencing of Wong Chi-fung in relation to the offence of “conspiracy to commit collusion with foreign countries or with external elements to endanger national security”.

The US Consulate General’s spokesperson made the comments in response to media enquiries on the sentencing.

In a statement, the Hong Kong SAR Government said the relevant remarks amounted to groundless attacks and smears, and to despicable political manipulation.

It urged the spokesperson to immediately cease making unconstructive and irresponsible remarks on the Hong Kong SAR’s work to safeguard national security, and to refrain from fabricating facts to mislead the public.

The statement highlighted that, before the implementation of the Hong Kong National Security Law (HKNSL), Wong Chi-fung, Law Kwun-chung, and others, persistently colluded with foreign countries and external elements, actively lobbied the US to pass legislation relating to Hong Kong, and openly solicited foreign countries to impose sanctions against China and the Hong Kong SAR.

In the case concerned, Wong pleaded guilty to the charge and the substance of the offence, including that he conspired with absconder Law Kwun-chung and others to solicit foreign countries and external elements, including the US, to impose sanctions against, blockade, or engage in other hostile activities against the People’s Republic of China and the Hong Kong SAR, and their officials. This included urging the US to revoke the special treatment enjoyed by Hong Kong as a Special Administrative Region under US law.

The statement said it is manifest that these acts endangered national security, and that the malicious intentions behind hostile actions by the US can been seen through by all.

It added that the court determined that Wong and Law were the masterminds in the case and the advocates at the forefront of calls for foreign countries to impose sanctions and hostile measures. Moreover, after the implementation of the HKNSL, they persisted in acts endangering national security.

The Hong Kong SAR Government, highlighting that the court sentenced Wong to 10 years’ imprisonment, said the reasons for this sentence were well-reasoned and sound. It said the court had explained that it was necessary to express the community’s abhorrence at the defendant’s acts in colluding with foreign forces or external elements to endanger national security, and to serve the imperative of deterrence.

Emphasising its constitutional duty to safeguard national security, the Government said it will continue to resolutely combat and pursue anti-China and destabilising elements, and agents of external forces. It added that it will ensure that laws are observed and strictly enforced, and that offenders are brought to account, so as to prevent, suppress and punish acts and activities endangering national security.

articles.title: CE attends import expo in Shanghai
articles.excerpt: The ninth China International Import Expo is being held from today until November 10 at the National Exhibition & Convention…
articles.fullText:
The ninth China International Import Expo is being held from today until November 10 at the National Exhibition & Convention Center in Shanghai, with Chief Executive John Lee attending the expo today.

A record high of over 400 Hong Kong enterprises are participating in this year's expo.

In the morning, Mr Lee attended the opening ceremony of the expo and the Hongqiao Forum. Later, he accompanied Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang in touring the Hong Kong exhibition area of the China Pavilion.

Under the theme “Connectivity & Enterprise”, the Hong Kong exhibition area showcases Hong Kong’s commitment to capitalising on its role as a bridge linking China and the world, and its multiple top rankings in global indexes.

Mr Lee attended the “Hong Kong Parallel Session” of the Hongqiao Forum in the afternoon. The session was jointly organised by the Hong Kong SAR Government and the Ministry of Commerce.

Mr Lee and Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao both delivered remarks at the session, while Vice Minister of Commerce Yan Dong also attended. Under the theme “Aligning with the National 15th Five-Year Plan, Serving the National Development, & Seizing New Opportunities for Hong Kong”, the session attracted around 400 participants.

Mr Lee remarked that this was the first large-scale briefing session held at an international forum since the Hong Kong SAR Government announced Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, which laid out the city's unique advantages of being strongly supported by its motherland and closely connected to the world under the “one country, two systems” principle.

He said Hong Kong will continue to play its role as a “super connector” and “super value-adder”, advance its development of “four centres and one hub”, and contribute its strengths towards building a great country.

After the session, Mr Lee toured the Enterprise & Business Exhibition and showed support for Hong Kong enterprises at the Hong Kong Food Pavilion and Hong Kong Services Pavilion, both set up by the Trade Development Council.

Together, the two pavilions are hosting 71 Hong Kong enterprises, with over 60% of these exhibiting for the first time this year, showcasing quality Hong Kong products and services across sectors such as food, finance, professional services, logistics and transportation, and innovation and technology (I&T).

Invest Hong Kong and the Tourism Board are also using the expo to promote Hong Kong’s advantages and its latest tourism offerings.

In the evening, Mr Lee hosted a networking dinner, where he exchanged views with political and business leaders from Hong Kong and the Mainland. He promoted Hong Kong's professional services and I&T sectors, and encouraged Mainland enterprises to make use of the city as a platform to “go global”.

articles.title: Man arrested under security law
articles.excerpt: The Police Force's National Security Department today arrested a 34-year-old local man in Mong Kok on suspicion of committing seditious…
articles.fullText:
The Police Force's National Security Department today arrested a 34-year-old local man in Mong Kok on suspicion of committing seditious acts.

The man was arrested for the offence of “importing a publication that has a seditious intention”, contravening the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance.

Following Police investigations, the man, a local company director, is suspected of importing seditious books into local bookstores with the intent to bring hatred, contempt or disaffection against the Central People’s Government and Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Under the authorisation of court warrants, Police searched the arrested man's residence and company. Seditious books, digital devices used to purchase seditious books, and documents were seized. The man is being detained for further enquiries.

articles.title: HK global education role grows
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Education Choi Yuk-lin spoke today at the World Class University Presidents Forum 2026, highlighting Hong Kong's growing strength…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Education Choi Yuk-lin spoke today at the World Class University Presidents Forum 2026, highlighting Hong Kong's growing strength, global voice and strategic vision as a premier international higher education hub. The two-day forum in Hong Kong concludes today.

Addressing the audience, Ms Choi noted that the forum gathered leaders and university presidents representing more than one-third of the world's top 50 universities. "Assembling such a distinguished constellation of global academic leadership strongly reaffirms Hong Kong's standing as an international education hub and significantly enhances the city's discourse power in the global educational arena," she said.

Ms Choi emphasised that Hong Kong's institutional strength is firmly rooted in academic excellence, robust national support and open connectivity. Citing the latest QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027, she pointed out that Hong Kong continues to set regional benchmarks with five local universities securing places among Asia's top 10.

Serving as a vital bridge between East and West, Hong Kong offers a fertile ecosystem characterised by internationalisation and diversification to bring global talent together, she said. The education chief added that the forum forms part of a strategic series of signature initiatives promoting the “Study in Hong Kong” brand worldwide, alongside major events like February’s Asia-Pacific Association for International Education Conference and Exhibition.

Elaborating on the forum's theme, "Higher Education Reimagined: Innovating for the Future", Ms Choi stressed that no matter how the global landscape evolves, universities remain fundamentally tied to economic development, societal well-being and human progress. She noted that world-leading institutions must stand at the forefront to guide this transformation as Hong Kong's educational landscape evolves.

The vision is being physically realised through the development of the Northern Metropolis University Town. The Education Bureau pointed out that under the "One Town, Five Elements" framework, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is building a holistic campus ecosystem integrating higher education, advanced research, market innovation, vibrant living spaces and top-tier talent.

Positioned at the gateway to the Chinese Mainland, the University Town will foster deep industry-academia-research integration, linking academic research directly with industry capabilities to serve national development under the 15th Five-Year Plan.

articles.title: Student assessment report released
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Examinations & Assessment Authority (HKEAA) has submitted the 2026 Territory-wide System Assessment (TSA) report to the Education…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Examinations & Assessment Authority (HKEAA) has submitted the 2026 Territory-wide System Assessment (TSA) report to the Education Bureau, the Government announced today.

The report said that the performance of Primary 3 and Secondary 3 students in the three major subjects ­– Chinese Language, English Language and Mathematics – remained generally steady this year, aligning closely with results from previous assessments.

The Education Bureau welcomed the findings, noting that schools broadly agree that the TSA report provides practical data and analysis regarding student performance. Combined with internal assessment results, this information enables schools to tailor their curriculum plans and instructional strategies to enhance learning effectiveness, fully reflecting the "Assessment for Learning" ethos.

Expressing its gratitude to the school sector, the bureau commended educators for continuously adopting diversified teaching strategies to cater to the varied needs of students and raise instructional effectiveness.

The HKEAA will soon distribute school-level data directly to primary and secondary schools for feedback on learning and teaching. Meanwhile, the bureau will host thematic seminars on "Promoting Assessment for Learning" next month to support schools in making effective use of assessment data to enhance outcomes.

articles.title: Judicial proceedings defended
articles.excerpt: (To watch the full media session with sign language interpretation, click here .) Secretary for Security Tang Ping-keung today issued…
articles.fullText:
(To watch the full media session with sign language interpretation, click here .)

Secretary for Security Tang Ping-keung today issued a condemnation of malicious attacks and smears launched by external forces in relation to the Wong Chi-fung case, stating that Wong was sentenced through fair and open judicial proceedings.

The High Court’s Court of First Instance this morning sentenced Wong to 10 years’ imprisonment for the offence of “conspiracy to commit collusion with foreign countries or with external elements to endanger national security”.

Meeting the media this afternoon, Mr Tang said the court had ruled that the case fell within the category of "an offence of a grave nature" and warranted severe punishment.

“I note that since the sentence of Wong, external forces have launched malicious attacks and smears regarding the present case," he said. “Those launching attacks against us are exactly the same external forces that Wong Chi-fung and Law Kwun-chung attempted to collude with. They must be strongly condemned, and Hong Kong citizens must recognise and acknowledge that clearly.

“In fact, Wong pleaded guilty, and Wong was sentenced through fair and open judiciary proceedings that fully demonstrated the rule of law that the courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region have consistently upheld.”

The security chief iterated that it is the constitutional duty of the Hong Kong SAR Government to safeguard national security, and that the Government will continue to resolutely combat actions that endanger national security.

“We will discuss with the Department of Justice to see if there is any need for appeal of the sentence,” he added.

articles.title: CEDD saddened by site accident
articles.excerpt: The Civil Engineering & Development Department has stated that it is deeply saddened by the passing of a contractor's staff…
articles.fullText:
The Civil Engineering & Development Department has stated that it is deeply saddened by the passing of a contractor's staff member at a work site on Trunk Road T4 in Sha Tin today, and extended its deepest condolences to the deceased's family.

At about 11am this morning, a 61-year-old female worker is suspected to have been struck by a construction vehicle while working at the site on Sha Tin Road near Pok Hong Estate. She was certified dead at the scene.

Following the incident, department representatives went to the site to learn about the situation. It instructed the project team to follow up on the incident, carry out a comprehensive review of safety procedures and measures, and offer appropriate assistance to the deceased's family.

Work at the site has been suspended. The department has instructed the contractor to carry out a thorough investigation into the incident. It will also render full assistance to other investigating departments.

Separately, the Labour Department said it was saddened by the death of the worker and expressed its deepest sympathy to the deceased’s family members.

articles.title: US trade deficit contracts slightly in September
articles.excerpt: The US trade deficit contracted slightly in September, government data there showed on Wednesday, hovering close to its widest since…
articles.fullText:
The US trade deficit contracted slightly in September, government data there showed on Wednesday, hovering close to its widest since March 2025, driven by capital and consumer goods imports and strong exports.

The trade gap in the world's largest economy decreased by 0.6 percent to US$105 billion, according to data from the US Commerce Department.

This was below the US$107.7 billion projected in a consensus forecast released on Marketwatch.

US trade flows have swung significantly since US President Donald Trump returned to the White House in January 2025, as businesses rushed to get ahead of his sweeping and fast changing tariffs on trading partners.

In September, US imports rose by 1.2 percent to US$426.6 billion, driven by computers and their accessories. Crude oil imports decreased by US$1.3 billion.

US exports climbed by 1.8 percent to US$321.5 billion, with oil, food and overall capital goods contributing to the increase.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: John Lee visits Shanghai to promote SAR businesses

Chief Executive John Lee arrived in Shanghai on Wednesday afternoon after visiting Beijing, where he attended the opening ceremony of the 29th Beijing Hong Kong Economic Cooperation Symposium.

In a Facebook post, Lee thanked representatives from the Ministry of Commerce, Beijing's Liaison Office in the SAR, and the Shanghai Municipal People's Government, as well as colleagues from the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Shanghai for meeting him at the airport.

Lee will attend the opening ceremony of the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) on Thursday.

"This year's CIIE has attracted participants from 162 countries, regions, and international organisations, with a total exhibition area exceeding 440,000 square metres," the post read.

The CE will also attend the Hongqiao International Economic Forum.

"There, I will highlight how Hong Kong is leveraging its unique strengths to integrate into and serve the nation's overall development, showcasing our achievements and opportunities."

Lee said Shanghai and Hong Kong share deep historical ties, with the SAR pushing ahead plans to establish a "sister port" relationship with Shanghai within this year.

He added that a pilot project for the mutual exchange of trade data was launched last month and is expected to benefit local small and medium-sized enterprises that export goods from the mainland.

Lee is also expected to meet with Shanghai officials to deepen cooperation before returning to Hong Kong on Friday.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: The Download: blended meat, restored sight, and the agentic web
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

These startups hope “blended” food will cut our appetite for red meat

In the fall of 2025, Jeff Dodge served hungry students steaming marinara sauce and meatballs. The students loved them: 92% of those who tried them wanted them on the menu. Few could guess that mushrooms had been mixed into the meat.

Dodge was testing a new product called 50/Cut from the company Joyn. The blend of seemingly simple ingredients—available as meatballs, burgers, and ground meat—could help solve one of the biggest challenges of the climate crisis: getting people to eat less meat, particularly beef.

Joyn is among a wave of startups creating “blended meat,” which combines plant proteins with the real deal. The logic: The best meat replacement is … better meat.

Get a taste of the startups betting on greener beef .

—Meghan McCarron

This implant can restore sight for patients with macular degeneration

More than 5 million people have an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) called geographic atrophy, in which retinal cells die off. Until now, no treatment could restore their vision. A system called PRIMA changes that.

It combines a retinal implant with camera-equipped eyeglasses to improve sight in patients who develop a blind spot in the middle of their vision. After training sessions, more than 80% of recipients could read, do crosswords, and use their phones.

Find out how the sight-restoring implant works .

—Linda Marsa

MIT Technology Review Narrated: The agentic web is here

In 2001, a decade after inventing the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision: an internet navigated by autonomous software agents that address our every need, without requiring us to muck about with browsers and search engines ourselves.

At the time, the idea seemed far-fetched. But a quarter-century on, AI agents are beginning to make it a reality. They can triage your inbox, do your grocery shopping, and even access your bank accounts.

This new era is being called the agentic web, and it will inevitably transform the internet.  Whether the human web survives this transition is anyone’s guess .

This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts . Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released.

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 Democrats have dealt tech billionaires a major midterm setback
The results could bring tougher scrutiny of AI and data centres. ( CNBC )
+ Musk poured millions into Texas, but both his candidates lost. ( Wired $)
+ Several winners promised to restrict data centre construction. ( FT $)
+ Stock futures slid as Democrats won big. ( NBC News )
+ The tech left said it’s ready to “wipe the floor.”  ( Vanity Fair $)

2 Google is shutting off Search for schools that reject AI
The company said AI and Search can no longer be untwined. ( CNN )
+ Critics accused Google of pressuring schools to adopt AI. ( NBC News )
+ AI is the end of search as we know it. ( MIT Technology Review )

3 The Binance hackers used fake job interviews in their record heist
They targeted an engineer through LinkedIn. ( NBC News )
+ Researchers had repeatedly warned about the tactics. ( TechCrunch )
+ The breach could boost demand for specialist crypto custodians. ( CNBC )

4 Materials maker 3M will pay $7.35 billion to settle “forever chemicals” lawsuits
The suits involve PFAS in firefighting foam. ( WSJ $)
+ New tech could help rid water of PFAS. ( MIT Technology Review )

5 Finland is opening a nuclear waste vault built to last 100,000 years
It will bury spent fuel 400 metres underground. ( New Scientist $)
+ It’s time to make new plans for nuclear waste . ( MIT Technology Review )

6 Russia wants underground data centers after Ukrainian strikes
Drone attacks have disrupted services used by millions. ( Ars Technica )

7 Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models’ identity
FlashProve uses cryptography to verify a model’s outputs. ( TechCrunch )
+ “Personhood credentials” could prove you’re human. ( MIT Technology Review )

8 Old jet engines are being scavenged to power data centers
But environmentalists warn they will produce more pollution. ( NYT $)

9 Dinosaur blood has been found in fossils for the first time
The discovery advances research into ancient biomolecules. ( Guardian )

10 Chernobyl’s dogs appear to be evolving
Scientists found differences linked to DNA repair and immunity. ( Wired $)

Quote of the day

“Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time ”

—Elon Musk tries to laugh off a costly loss on X after the Republican candidates he spent record sums supporting got drubbed in the US midterm elections.

One more thing

Want to understand the current state of AI? Check out these charts.

If you’re following AI news, you’re probably getting whiplash. AI is a gold rush. AI is a bubble. AI is taking your job. AI can’t even read a clock. Stanford’s 2026 AI Index—the field’s annual report card—cuts through the noise.

The data reveals a technology evolving faster than we can manage. From the China-US rivalry and model breakthroughs to public sentiment and the impact on jobs, here are the index’s key findings on the state of AI today .

—Michelle Kim

We can still have nice things

A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line .)

articles.title: RTHK signs MoU with Tianjin Haihe Media Group
articles.excerpt: Radio Television Hong Kong (RTHK) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Tianjin Haihe Media Group, in a bid…
articles.fullText:
Radio Television Hong Kong (RTHK) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Tianjin Haihe Media Group, in a bid to boost bilateral collaboration in areas such as talent exchange and events.

The MoU was signed during a four-day trip by Director of Broadcasting Angelina Kwan to the mainland, which ended on Wednesday.

During the trip, Kwan, as well as participants of RTHK's national studies programme, called on the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the State Council, and met Deputy Director Zhang Dongmei.

Kwan also visited the National Radio and Television Administration and the Beijing Radio and Television Station to explore opportunities for strengthening exchange and co-operation.

On Tuesday, Kwan signed an MoU with Tianjin Haihe Media Group President Ma Bo. The two sides agreed to establish a framework for bilateral collaboration spanning programme resources, talent exchanges, co-operation on platform and copyright licensing, as well as on-ground events.

RTHK said the the partnership will facilitate the distribution of its content to the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, while enabling Tianjin Haihe Media Group's productions to reach international audiences through RTHK's platforms.

RTHK has signed MoUs with eight mainland and overseas media organisations so far this year.

"By building a growing network of broadcaster partnerships and deepening collaboration on an ongoing basis, RTHK is giving concrete expression to its strategic commitment to leveraging Hong Kong's unique role as a connector between the Chinese mainland and the wider world, thereby enhancing Hong Kong's international communication capacity and sharing the stories of the nation and Hong Kong on the global stage," a statement read.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Securing the agentic enterprise with data lineage
articles.excerpt: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing…
articles.fullText:
A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep. No human checks either handoff. When it’s discovered that the proposal includes unapproved, confidential, and sensitive information, no one can trace where the problematic data entered the workflow or how it spread across systems, files, and agents.

DOWNLOAD THE REPORT

This scenario illustrates why AI governance needs to evolve, rapidly and dynamically. As more enterprises begin to use agentic AI in daily workflows, they’re realizing that they must manage more than static files; they must manage moving and fragmented data that is continuously ingested, copied, summarized, transformed, reused, and redistributed in new forms. In short, AI security isn’t a tool problem; it’s a data visibility problem.

Consequently, traditional security approaches built solely around applications, systems, networks, or endpoints are no longer sufficient. Securing agentic AI at scale requires understanding how data moves. Teams, therefore, need to establish data lineage in order to effectively manage governance, accountability, and trust across human, agentic, and hybrid workflows.

Download the report

articles.title: HK, mainland stocks post gains
articles.excerpt: Stock markets mostly rose on Wednesday as investors assessed the impact of a Democratic sweep of the US Congress that…
articles.fullText:
Stock markets mostly rose on Wednesday as investors assessed the impact of a Democratic sweep of the US Congress that dealt a blow to Donald Trump's economic agenda as he heads into his final two years as president.

In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index gained ground for the fourth straight day, putting on 393 points or 1.67 percent to 23,919.

Mainland shares climbed as well, with the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index up 2.16 percent to 3,686 and the Shenzhen Component Index surging 4.22 percent to 11,335.

Across the region, the Nikkei in Japan fell 1.42 percent to 62,188, dragged down by tech stocks, whereas the South Korean Kospi finished 0.62 percent higher at 5,683.

The prospect of Congress coming to a standstill weighed on the US dollar and Treasury yields, with observers pointing out that such a scenario would restrict spending.

"Democratic control of Congress will make it harder for the White House administration to pass major partisan legislation. That could reduce the prospect of significant additional fiscal stimulus over the next two years," wrote David Chao at Invesco.

"For Asia, the implications matter. Less fiscal stimulus could reduce upward pressure on US growth, inflation and Treasury yields, potentially easing some of the pressure that higher US rates and a stronger dollar have placed on Asian currencies and monetary policy." (AFP/Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: China 'will continue working with US' after midterms
articles.excerpt: The Foreign Ministry on Wednesday said China was "willing to continue working" with the United States following midterm elections that…
articles.fullText:
The Foreign Ministry on Wednesday said China was "willing to continue working" with the United States following midterm elections that saw US President Donald Trump's Republicans lose control of both chambers of Congress.

"The midterm elections are an internal affair of the United States," Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told a regular news briefing in Beijing.

"China is willing to continue working with the US to uphold and implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, strengthen communication, properly manage differences, expand cooperation, and build a constructive, strategically stable China-US relationship based on the principles of respect, fairness, and reciprocity."

In Europe, French Finance Minister Roland Lescure said Trump remained in charge on foreign policy issues despite the GOP's defeats in the midterms, adding that the American leader was unpredictable.

"Either he decides to rise above the fray — acknowledging that changes are necessary, particularly regarding gasoline prices, which directly affect people — and, I might add, he tones down his international involvement; or he does not," Lescure said in an interview on French TV channel BFM.

"Frankly, this is something we will need to keep an eye on in the coming days," he added.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on Wednesday that voters in the United States had rejected policies that "only impoverish", as well as hate, sexism and climate change denialism following Republican defeats.

Sanchez said the far-right wave that had buoyed conservative movements on both sides of the Atlantic was "collapsing" rather than growing.

In Africa, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said that the results from the midterms would "introduce a new era in world relations".

"We have seen that the Democrats have taken control of the Senate and of the House, and the people of America have spoken," Ramaphosa told reporters. (Agencies)

articles.title: CE calls for closer cooperation with nation's capital
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee on Wednesday called for closer financial and innovative ties with the city of Beijing, as he…

Chief Executive John Lee on Wednesday called for closer financial and innovative ties with the city of Beijing, as he continued his visit to the capital.

Speaking at a symposium on Beijing-Hong Kong cooperation, Lee said finance had been a key area for collaboration between the two cities over the years.

He called for promoting two-way financial opening-up to facilitate economic transformation.

“Hong Kong, as an international financial centre, connects mainland markets and global capital,” he said.

“It acts as the most convenient international financing platform for enterprises in Beijing.

“Through cross-border fund management, wealth management and a network connecting global investors, it serves enterprises’ needs for business expansion.”

Lee said the two cities would continue to serve two-way financing for enterprises, and jointly expand green and sustainable finance, as well as offshore renminbi business.

He also expressed hope of deepening innovative cooperation between the SAR and Beijing, as the nation developed new quality productive forces and promoted technological revolution and industrial transformation.

The innovation sectors in the two cities would promote collaboration in life and health technology, artificial intelligence and robotics, he said.

Lee added that Hong Kong would continue to assist mainland enterprises in going global.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Yau highlights benefits of RCEP accession for HK

Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development Algernon Yau said Hong Kong's entry into the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership could inject fresh impetus into advancing the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP) agenda.

"We welcome the establishment of the Accession Working Group for Hong Kong in September this year, and hope that our accession could inject fresh impetus into advancing the FTAAP agenda," he said during a virtual meeting at the 37th Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) Ministerial Meeting held on Tuesday.

Yau said that enhancing economic integration has been the core objective of Apec, and that one of the directions is to continue to advance the FTAAP.

He called on member economies to continue to strengthen connectivity in various areas, enabling the efficient flow of goods, services, capital and people, while narrowing development gaps and creating opportunities for all sectors across the region.

Yau also stressed that the multilateral trading system must remain the foundation of regional integration and international trade, highlighting the importance of enhancing co-operation to deal with the seismic changes in the trade landscape.

articles.title: HK offers businesses growth and capital: FS
articles.excerpt: Financial Secretary Paul Chan said Hong Kong is well-placed to provide businesses with both growth opportunities and long-term capital. The…
articles.fullText:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan said Hong Kong is well-placed to provide businesses with both growth opportunities and long-term capital.

The finance chief made his remarks on Wednesday during a conversation session with investors on the second day of the Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit in Central.

Chan noted that a company needs different forms of capital at each stage of development to turn its potential into sustained growth.

This, he said, is exactly where Hong Kong comes into play.

“Under the 'One Country, Two Systems' framework, Hong Kong is closely connected to the Chinese mainland, while a common law legal system, free flow of capital and international networks provide a trusted and familiar environment for global investors to take part in China's enormous growth,” Chan said.

“Here, we already bring together venture capital, private equity, family offices and asset managers, with deep equity and bond markets. Our task is to connect them more closely across the corporate life cycle.”

He said follow-on fundraising on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange reached HK$570 billion in the first nine months of the year, showing that the city’s market continues to support companies well beyond their initial listings.

Chan also said the aim is to expand allocation choices to help investors manage risks and liquidity in support of long-term value creation.

Hong Kong will keep raising its market efficiency with faster approvals, streamlined processes and clearer frameworks for new financial products – all without compromising its integrity, he added.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Myanmar opposition forces hopeful that U.S. strategy could bring about peace
articles.excerpt: Washington’s framework includes peacemaking to increase regional influence and provide access to rare earths.
articles.fullText:
Updated at 11:30 a.m. ET on Nov. 4, 2026.
Read a version of this story in Burmese
Armed ethnic groups and members of Myanmar’s shadow government are hoping that a recently made public U.S. strategy for their country decrease fighting and bring about peace with the military-backed government, the organizations told Radio Free Asia.
The U.S. State Department recently released an Integrated Country Strategy document for Myanmar that outlines Washington’s aims to use diplomacy to promote peace in the volatile Southeast Asian country, potentially providing access to rare earth deposits dominated by China.
The policy document lays out four mission goals, which include protecting U.S. citizens, addressing trade deficits, promoting peace, and increasing U.S. regional influence through engagement.
Lwe River network, Mekong Tributary, with clusters of rare earth mines in Shan State, Myanmar, Nov. 11, 2025.
(Planet Labs via Reuters) To achieve these goals, dealing with Myanmar’s military-backed government – headed by the same people who ousted the previous government in a coup in 2021 – cannot be avoided. Washington initially shunned engagement with the military after the coup and imposed sanctions on its most senior leaders, but has since softened its stance, rolling back some sanctions and even holding high level talks in September 2026.
A U.S. State Department spokesperson on Tuesday explained the shift to RFA.
“The Administration has been evaluating how to calibrate Washington’s policy towards Burma to achieve regional stability, and also make progress on key U.S. priorities and has determined that wholesale disengagement with the authorities in Naypyidaw countered U.S. strategic interests in Burma and the region. We are pursuing a policy that welcomes dialogue with all stakeholders involved in the conflict as we encourage Burma to make progress on key U.S. priorities, including addressing scam centers, improving the domestic operating environment for U.S. businesses, and building towards a genuine peace process that stabilizes the country.”
Riot police man a barrier in front of the Yangon City Hall on Feb. 6, 2021, in Yangon, Myanmar.
(Getty Images) David Gum Awng, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs for the National Unity Government, or NUG, a shadow government made up of former government officials who were ousted in the 2021 coup, told RFA he understood the realities of the situation.
“The NUG respects and acknowledges that the U.S. government is actively engaging in Myanmar affairs and formulating a strategy aimed at peace, economy, and regional stability. The NUG will continue to engage in discussions with the U.S. government, Congress, and the international community including relevant partner nations.
We will also continue to urge that the U.S. government’s policies and practical actions towards Myanmar support the democratic and federal aspirations of the Myanmar people, address the root causes of the conflict, and lead toward an inclusive political resolution. International engagement in Myanmar affairs should not prolong the military dictatorship, but should aim to bring about genuine political change based on the will and rights of the people after escaping from this bad system.”
Kyaw Ni, Deputy Minister of Home Affairs and Immigration for the NUG, shared his opinion that amidst the policies of superpower nations, one must strive to achieve benefits for one’s own country.
“In this policy shift of a superpower nation, small countries suffer a lot, so a country undergoing revolution like Burma suffers even more. It is likely to be affected. Since these are superpower nations, they write policies based on their own interests. So our public also has to struggle among these policies to reach our desired revolutionary goal without harming the interests of our country, our people, and our revolution.”
The Chin National Front (CNF) soldiers in an undated photo.
(Chin Information Center) Salai Htet Ni, spokesperson for the Chin National Front, an armed ethnic rebel group, said the U.S. government needs to understand the underlying problems in Myanmar politics and get deeply involved.
“The U.S. government needs to understand the military junta’s unjust violence and killing of the people. They need to consider that. On our part, if they can perform first-stage actions like humanitarian aid for war refugees and addressing violent attacks and killings, we would welcome the U.S. involvement even more.”
Another ethnic armed group, — the Karen National Union — said U.S. involvement might reduce the amount of internal fighting, spokesperson Saw Kler Say told RFA on Wednesday.
“The new U.S. strategy could bring about changes or have a specific impact on our country from a military perspective. Firstly, it might lead to a situation where the military junta is compelled to stop its attacks targeting the civilian population.
Secondly, the U.S. might take steps — or offer recommendations — aimed at halting the ongoing internal conflicts. Politically, we also believe they are likely envisioning a political landscape that is acceptable to all parties—one that would include both the detained opposition leaders and the revolutionary forces.
To achieve sustainable peace in Myanmar by 2030, the first step must be to cease attacks targeting the civilian population. The next step involves reaching a consensus on a dialogue process aimed at ending internal conflicts; only through such a mutually agreed-upon framework can a ceasefire be attained.
In addition to these measures, all detained opposition leaders and political prisoners must be released. Without these actions, I believe that any dialogue will be extremely difficult. If detained political prisoners are excluded, meaning the process fails to be truly all inclusive, then a successful outcome may well be entirely impossible.
Regarding the emergence of a federal democracy in Myanmar, the new U.S. strategy presents both positive opportunities and concerning risks. On one hand, it could potentially lead to a genuine transition toward a federal democracy—for instance, by facilitating the abolition of the 2008 Constitution and the drafting and adoption of a new federal constitution. On the other hand, there is a risk that if the discourse is driven solely by U.S. interests, the path toward the federal democracy we envision could be diverted, creating significant challenges."
Representatives of the Kachin Independence Army and the Arakan Army responded that they were not ready to comment.
Arakan Army soldiers in an undated photo.
(Arakan Army) The Arakan Army’s Khaing Thukha asked that questions be channeled through official emails.
Hla Thein, spokesperson for the Union Solidarity and Development Party – formed by former military officers – told RFA that the U.S. strategy document is constructive for mutual interest and should be welcomed.
“Big nations becoming interested in our country, interested from a positive and beneficial perspective, should be welcomed no matter what. We have no permanent friends and no permanent enemies. If they come to cooperate fairly for our country’s interest, our people’s interest, and national interest, we will warmly welcome them.”
RFA attempted to contact Khaing Khaing Soe, spokesperson for the military government’s presidential office, but received no reply.
Col. Saw Kyaw Nyunt, spokesperson for the 7 EAO Alliance of ethnic armed organizations that have individually signed a Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement with the military, said the shift in U.S. attitude might be due to an understanding of Myanmar’s needs.
“In attempting to restart the peace process, international support and assistance are needed. The shift in attitude by the U.S. toward the peace process is likely because they realized that peace is urgently needed due to Myanmar’s reality. By 2030, which is in three or four years, seeking ways to build sustainable peace during that period can be viewed as assessing and speaking on our country’s needs.”
Salai Shein Tun, a secretariat member of the Chin National League for Democracy Party, which won a single seat in Myanmar’s parliament in the 2020 general election, told RFA that the new U.S. policy might face challenges from competitors.
“Speaking of challenges, the challenge from China as a big power is strong. Inside Myanmar and within ethnic regions, the challenge is also strong. In areas bordering neighboring China, they approach with a Chinese style model, whereas looking at the western side, in Chin, Kachin, and Rakhine states, they emphasize federalism. The country they connect with is India … Areas connected with neighboring China do not talk about federalism. Discussions will take quite a bit of effort when those following the Chinese model want to negotiate with the domestic groups that follow the federal model.”
According to the Integrated Country Strategy document, the released text was approved by the Trump administration on Aug. 31, 2026, before the mid-September secret visit to Naypyidaw by Michael Vance, the assistant secretary of state for intelligence and research.
Vance also led at least 12 U.S. government officials during a second round of talks with Myanmar military government officials in Tokyo in the second week of October.
Edited by Eugene Whong.
Update includes comments from Saw Kler Say.

articles.title: PSG crush Villarreal in Champions League; Barca cruise
articles.excerpt: Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain scored four times in the first 17 minutes on their way to a 6-0 demolition of…
articles.fullText:
Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain scored four times in the first 17 minutes on their way to a 6-0 demolition of Villarreal in Spain in the Champions League on Tuesday, as the French side shrugged off injuries to key players to maintain their perfect record in the competition this season.

Joao Neves, Desire Doue, Senny Mayulu and Fabian Ruiz all struck at the Estadio de la Ceramica as PSG set a record for the fastest team to score four times in a match in Europe'e elite club competition.

Ruiz added another early in the second half and teenager David Boly completed a comprehensive demolition of the side that finished third in La Liga last season.

"I obviously wasn't expecting that but you get matches where you start in that way," PSG's Spanish coach Luis Enrique told broadcaster Canal Plus.

"We were impressive throughout and we are really pleased even if it is very difficult for Villarreal. But it is hard when you play against a team like us that presses constantly."

PSG have lost star winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for the rest of the campaign after he suffered a torn ACL in his right knee in last month's win over Barcelona, while Ousmane Dembele, with captain Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes are also missing.

Despite that, the Ligue 1 leaders made it 10 straight wins in all competitions, including four in the Champions League as they aim to lift the European Cup for a third season running.

They are the only team to have maximum points after four matches in this year's Champions League.

Liverpool, Real Madrid and Real Betis all have maximum points from three games before playing on Wednesday, and Luis Enrique's prolific side have now scored 20 goals on that run.

Like all matches in the Champions League on Tuesday, a minute's silence was held prior to kick-off in tribute to Jesus de Miguel, the Tenerife player who died following a collision in a Spanish second-division game on Monday.

The poignant silence was also held to remember the victims of last week's deadly train crash in Spain, in which 69 people were killed.

Meanwhile, Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa, ending the English side's perfect start to the competition.

Five-time winners Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goalscoring form with a second-half brace.

Barca bounced back after defeat by champions Paris Saint-Germain in their previous European outing to stay in the hunt for a top eight league phase berth.

Unai Emery's Villa competed well in the first half but were eventually undone by Barca's greater ability in the final third.

The Champions League anthem was not played before the game, as a mark of respect for Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel, who died on Tuesday morning after an on-pitch collision in a Spanish second division match the previous day, provoking shock across the football world.

"Yes it was (a good win), I want to dedicate this win to the fans, but today I don't want to talk about football, I want to send a message to the family of Jesus. May he rest in peace," Raphinha told Movistar.

"This can happen to anyone, it's very tough... you're going to play a game and the same thing can happen to you...

"From the club, I want to send a message of strength to the family."

Villa captain John McGinn had only visited the Camp Nou once previously, on a summer holiday as an eight-year-old, and might have expected better weather than the downpour both teams were subjected to.

The skipper might also have expected a more focused start, with Villa handing Barcelona the lead in the seventh minute.

The Spanish champions pressed Aston Villa extremely high and Joao Gomes played a poor pass straight to Yamal in his own box. The 19-year-old winger gladly took the gift and stroked past Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki.

"Tonight was a huge learning curve for us and I am sure it will stand us in good stead for the future," McGinn told TNT Sports.

"Barcelona made the right decisions at the right times and scored really good goals."

Yamal's goal was his 14th in the competition across his career, beating Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe's previous record tally of 13 netted as a teenager in the Champions League.

Emery, who endured one of the worst nights of his career away at Barca when helming PSG in 2017 during a 6-1 defeat, may have feared the worst.

However Villa reacted strongly and Matty Cash had a vicious drive deflected narrowly wide before Joao Cancelo blocked Gomes's effort.

Suzuki saved from Anthony Gordon as Villa again struggled to bring the ball out from the back under Barca's pressing.

Garcia was called into action again by Johan Manzambi as the match lurched from end-to-end.

Barcelona extended their lead early in the second half when Fermin Lopez fed Raphinha, who showed quick footwork before finding the bottom corner.

Cancelo set up Raphinha for Barcelona's third with a superb cross with the outside of his boot. The Brazil winger, who has made the number nine position his own this season, pounced from close range for his 19th goal across all competitions.

Yamal sent a shot skidding wide as Barcelona probed for a fourth. It did not come, but the Catalan giants were able to record a first Champions League clean sheet in 19 games. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: West Ham eye Parker move after sacking Nuno
articles.excerpt: West Ham are expected to hire Scott Parker as their new manager after the Championship club sacked Nuno Espirito Santo…
articles.fullText:
West Ham are expected to hire Scott Parker as their new manager after the Championship club sacked Nuno Espirito Santo on Tuesday.

Parker is believed to be West Ham's top choice to replace Nuno and could be appointed in time for Wednesday's match against Cardiff after opening talks with the club.

The former England midfielder spent four seasons as a player with West Ham and led Bournemouth and Burnley to promotion from the Championship as a manager.

Parker, 46, also had spells in charge at Fulham and Club Brugge.

West Ham are looking for their fourth permanent boss since David Moyes left in May 2024.

Julen Lopetegui was sacked after just six months in charge and Graham Potter was axed after only eight months in charge.

Nuno, 52, oversaw the Hammers' relegation from the Premier League last season but stayed with the east London club in a bid to lead them back into the top flight.

Many viewed the Hammers as favourites to win automatic promotion, but they are currently eighth in the second-tier table, six points behind leaders Middlesbrough, after 13 games.

West Ham had lost their past two league games against Southampton and West Brom.

Nuno, who previously managed Wolves, Tottenham and Nottingham Forest, was appointed in September last year.

"West Ham United can confirm that men's first-team head coach Nuno Espirito Santo has left his position with immediate effect," the club said in a statement.

"Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the board of directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club's objectives and expectations remain on track." (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Man Utd snap winless run with Roma comeback
articles.excerpt: Manchester United roared back from 2-0 down to give beleaguered manager Michael Carrick a lifeline with a memorable 3-2 win…
articles.fullText:
Manchester United roared back from 2-0 down to give beleaguered manager Michael Carrick a lifeline with a memorable 3-2 win over Roma at Old Trafford in the Champions League.

The unrest among the home fans bordered on mutiny after Roma surged into a 2-0 lead inside 20 minutes through Matias Soule and Donyell Malen.

But United ended a nine-game winless run in all competitions thanks to Matheus Cunha's double after a twice-taken Bruno Fernandes penalty had reduced the deficit.

"This place does incredible things, does magical things," said Carrick.

"I spoke with them at half-time a little bit about how this place can change and it only takes one moment. It certainly did that and the boys made every little bit of every little opportunity. Fantastic in the end."

The decision to hand Carrick a stay of execution looked to have backfired in a lifeless first half United performance.

Roma, though, failed to slay their ghosts of four previous defeats at Old Trafford in another spectacular Champions League collapse.

Gian Piero Gasperini's men lost 4-3 to Real Madrid last month after leading 3-1 with just eight minutes remaining.

"A game lasts 90 minutes," said Gasperini. "They stepped it up in the second half but we could have done more to safeguard the score."

Carrick reacted to Lisandro Martinez's foolish red card in a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday by dropping the Argentine international.

It made little difference as his disorganised defence was torn apart inside the opening 20 minutes.

Soule was afforded acres of space to control Rodrigo Mora's pass and slot past Senne Lammens on 11 minutes.

Moments later United were left completely exposed again down their left and Malen converted a penalty after Soule's shot hit the outstretched hand of Ayden Heaven.

The game was temporarily stopped midway through the first half by supporters throwing tennis balls onto the field, accompanied by chants calling for with United's unpopular owners, the American-based Glazer family, to sell the club.

United were dealt a further blow inside two minutes of the second half when £70 million signing Carlos Baleba pulled up with a suspected severe hamstring injury after bursting into the Roma box.

Yet, Carrick's luck turned just before the hour mark when Cunha won a generous penalty award for minimal contact by Gianluca Mancini.

Fernandes's first spot-kick was saved by Roma's third-choice goalkeeper Devis Vasquez, but was given a reprieve by encroaching by the visitors.

The United captain smashed home at the second attempt to kickstart the comeback.

Seconds later Bryan Mbeumo hit the inside of both posts after being played in by Cunha.

United were gifted the equaliser seven minutes from time when Leonardo Balerdi's swipe at fresh air gave Cunha the simplest task to tap in.

Three minutes later, the Brazilian thundered a shot past Vasquez at his near post and flung himself into the crowd in what proved to be a costly celebration.

Cunha was booked and then shown a second yellow card moments later for a wild lunge in stoppage time.

But the 10 men held on to breathe new life into United's Champions League campaign after back-to-back defeats against Atletico Madrid and Como.

Whether it proves to be a turning point or just another temporary reprieve for Carrick remains to be seen.

"It's one game, so it depends on what happens next and we've got to capitalise on that," added Carrick.

"To see the supporters going home happy, it's what we live for. To give them performances and nights like this." (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Top Uni presidents forum opens
articles.excerpt: The World Class University Presidents Forum 2026 opened today on the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology campus. The…
articles.fullText:
The World Class University Presidents Forum 2026 opened today on the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology campus.

The two-day forum, themed “Higher Education Reimagined: Innovating for the Future”, brings together in Hong Kong presidents and senior leadership figures from around 50 world-leading universities to explore strategic directions for the development of global higher education.

As a premier event in the global education community fully supported by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government and hosted by the HKUST, the forum highlights Hong Kong’s unique strengths and its pivotal status as a bridge connecting the Chinese Mainland with the global higher education system.

Officiating at the opening ceremony, Acting Chief Executive Chan Kwok-ki noted in his speech that higher education has long been a vital pillar of Hong Kong’s success and a cornerstone of its role as a hub for global talent and academic exchange.

He highlighted that Hong Kong is the only city in the world to host five universities in the global top 100 – a testament to the strength of its higher education sector, which is further underscored by the latest QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027.

The Hong Kong SAR Government will continue to align closely with national strategies, accelerate the integrated development of education, technology and talent, and further consolidate Hong Kong’s status as an international hub for post-secondary education through initiatives such as the development of the Northern Metropolis University Town.

Several heavyweight interuniversity co-operation signing ceremonies took place during the event, marking important strategic co-operation agreements between leading institutions and organisations at home and abroad. These included a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on deepening collaboration between Central South University and Monash University; an MOU between Zhejiang University and the HKUST on establishing a joint innovation centre; a Trilateral Joint Seed Fund agreement among the University of Warwick, Nanyang Technological University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University; and a student exchange agreement between Trinity College Dublin and Nanjing University, marking a new milestone in global higher education and research collaborative innovation.

Today’s topics include “The University and the Century Ahead”, “Educating the Human: The Generation Shaping the Intelligent Age”, and “From Ideas to Innovation: Universities Driving the Future Economy”.

A number of prominent leaders from the political, business and academic sectors addressed the forum either in person or via video message, including the eighth Secretary-General of the United Nations Ban Ki-moon, President of the 43rd session of the General Conference of UNESCO Khondker M Talha, President of the China Association of Higher Education Lin Huiqing, HKUST Council Chairman Harry Shum, and HKUST President Nancy Ip.

articles.title: The Download: controlling AI agents and “Super Intelligence” loyalty tests
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check

A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules.

While game theory predicts how rational actors behave under particular rules, reverse game theory designs rules to elicit the behavior we want. Think of splitting a cake: if one person cuts it and the other gets first choice, the cutter has an incentive to make the portions equal.

Researchers believe the approach could align AI more closely with our rules and instructions. But big questions remain about whether these mechanisms will work in practice.

Here’s how reverse game theory could help make AI agents behave .

—Amit Katwala

Here’s who is falling in line for Trump’s “Super Intelligence” loyalty test

At the end of September, President Trump signed an executive order with just one directive: government agencies must rebrand artificial intelligence as “Super Intelligence.”

One month on, the rebrand is slowly appearing across government websites and documents, but it hasn’t caught on with everyone. Even some of the biggest names in tech still use “AI.”

But the bigger concern is the new term becoming a political loyalty test: Those who use it signal allegiance to the administration. Those who don’t become targets for attacks.

So one month in, who’s on board?

—James O’Donnell

This story is from The Algorithm, our weekly AI newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Monday.

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 Today’s midterms will test AI’s influence on US politics
Candidates are betting that AI regulation will sway voters to their side. ( Axios )
+ Angry constituents could derail Elon Musk’s Republican bets. ( BI )
+ Tech investors are on edge about the results. ( Reuters $)
+ America is divided over AI regulation. ( MIT Technology Review )

2 Nvidia is ordering data centre clients to limit their business with China 
It told providers that the majority of their sales must be non-Chinese. ( FT $)
+ The move follows pressure from Washington. ( Bloomberg $)
+ Chinese AI has ruptured the White House. ( MIT Technology Review )

3 Hackers have turned supermarket fridges into a food security risk
Attacks in Europe have put US supermarket systems on alert. ( CNBC )
+ They’ve also sparked concerns over other domestic appliances. ( BBC )
+ It’s a good time for doing crime. ( MIT Technology Review )

4 Scientists have detected signals at the smallest scale ever explored
The discovery offers clues to a world of exotic new particles. ( BBC )
+ It came via CERN’s Large Hadron Collider. ( The Times $)

5 Zapping part of the brain makes you think harder—at a cost
It can both improve performance and reduce motivation. ( New Scientist $)
+ Neuropixels probes are transforming how we study the brain. ( Nature )

6 Big tech is splurging on mega gas plants to power data centers
The projectsthreaten to reverse years of climate pledges. ( WP $)

7 Google says an Android partner infected 1.3 million devices
The malware infected TV boxes and other Android-based devices. ( Verge )

8 Apple is trying to create its first robot
It’s proving a lot harder than expected, though. ( Information $)
+ AI robots are still a long way from useful. ( MIT Technology Review )

9 China’s biggest shopping festival has a new product to sell: AI
AI tokens have become a major new Singles’ Day category. ( Reuters $)

10 A meteorite in the Sahara has revealed new clues about Mars
Its chemistry may help explain how the planet lost its water. ( Wired $)

Quote of the day

“Don’t spend money unduly by asking a human expert to enter into a debate with a robot expert.”

—Steven Benmor, a family lawyer, tells the Wall Street Journal that clients increasingly need to pay human experts to correct advice they’ve received from chatbots.

One more thing

The noise we make is hurting animals. Can we learn to shut up?

As human society has expanded, animals have started struggling to hear one another. For many birds, the noise has grown so loud that they’ve begun to sing with faster trills. Now, their mating calls aren’t as effective.

The growing hubbub can also increase bird-on-bird conflict, and entire species that can’t handle urban clamor simply leave town for good. But there are technological solutions to the noises hurting animals—and they could help humans, too.

Read the full story .

—Clive Thompson

We can still have nice things

A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line .)

articles.title: Spanish footballer dies after collision with keeper
articles.excerpt: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died on Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in a sickening collision with…
articles.fullText:
Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died on Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in a sickening collision with FC Andorra's goalkeeper in a Spanish second division match.

"Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe this is real, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death...of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," his club Tenerife said in a statement.

"No words can ease the pain, nothing can lessen this great feeling of sadness. Our thoughts are with the family, his close friends and Tenerife fans, who today are grieving over this terrible news."

De Miguel, 30, was fouled in the middle of the pitch by Equatorial Guinea international goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his goal.

The incident happened towards the end of the match, which was tied at 2-2. Owono was sent off and the match was subsequently abandoned.

Spanish media said that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated, with Tenerife later saying the player's condition had "worsened neurologically", before his death.

De Miguel had been at Tenerife for just over a season, having joined in the summer of 2025 from Castellon.

"I am so deeply sorry. Rest in peace, Jesus," former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, Andorra's majority shareholder, wrote on social media.

Andorra also sent their "most sincere condolences" to De Miguel's family, team-mates and Tenerife.

Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atletico Madrid and other clubs in Spain also sent messages of condolence, as well as the Spanish football federation.

"Shattered by this sad news, the Royal Spanish Football Federation wishes to express our deepest sorrow at his passing today," wrote the federation in a statement. (AFP)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Collaboration is key to development, Nobel winner says
articles.excerpt: An Australian astronomer and Nobel laureate has called on fellow researchers to share their results and foster collaboration, in line…
articles.fullText:
An Australian astronomer and Nobel laureate has called on fellow researchers to share their results and foster collaboration, in line with the spirit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) to break down barriers.

World leaders are expected to gather in Shenzhen later this month for the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting. China, as host member nation, has outlined three core priorities: openness, innovation, and cooperation.

Those are also values that Brian Schmidt has been advocating for years.

An astrophysicist by profession, he won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2011 for the discovery of the accelerating expansion of the universe.

Schmidt then became vice-chancellor of the Australian National University in 2016. During his eight-year tenure, he discovered the importance of having a suitable environment for students to turn their concepts into tangible results.

He said Shenzhen is the place to be for researchers.

"I'm from Canberra in Australia. There is almost certainly not going to be the pieces in Canberra for me to say, 'I've got this idea, let me take and make a prototype'," he told Shenzhen Media Group in an interview.

"And Shenzhen, every one of those pieces is there – the drone manufacturer, I need a camera manufacturer, I need an AI integrator, and I can just kind of go through and put it together.

"Which means that developing an idea into a prototype, you can do just phenomenally fast in Shenzhen compared to literally any place in the world."

While Shenzhen offers the ingredients to accelerate scientific development, Schmidt says the people involved in it must be willing to share their knowledge for the research community to thrive.

"It's really easy to start saying all this basic research is really valuable; therefore we don't share it. But that means that we all have to reinvent it, we don't get to work together, we don't get to know each other, and the whole thing just kind of... no one ends up with anything," he explained.

He encouraged researchers to collaborate, especially at a time when countries and blocs are drawing up trade barriers.

"Because there's many, many barriers going up right now. So Apec is trying to lower those barriers. So it's really important that we keep focusing on that, because if we focus [on] how, you know, you might take my idea, and I might take your idea, then we don't work together."

At a recent forum in Beijing, Schmidt also urged scientists to cooperate wherever they could to solve global sustainability issues.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Mideast conflict forces postponement of Asian Cup
articles.excerpt: The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has postponed the 2027 Asian Cup by almost a year because of the conflict in…
articles.fullText:
The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has postponed the 2027 Asian Cup by almost a year because of the conflict in the Middle East and recent deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.

The AFC issued a statement on Tuesday saying after extensive consultations with Saudi organisers it had decided to push the tournament kickoff back from January 7 to December 23.

The organising committee “approved to reschedule the flagship national team tournament in light of the current exceptional circumstances arising from developments in the region, including substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions,” the AFC said in a statement.

“Exceptional circumstances have been created for the organisation and delivery of the competition as originally scheduled, making the postponement necessary in the interest of all participating teams, officials, spectators and other stakeholders.”

The new dates — December 23, 2027 to January 21, 2028 — will be submitted to Fifa for approval.

The decision to delay the tournament ends months of speculation about a postponement which, until recently, had been rejected by local organisers.

As recently as last week, Saudi officials released the kickoff times and finalised schedule for the 2027 tournament in a move aimed at assuring continental football federations that planning was on track.

Muhammed Q. Alghamdi, a spokesman for the organising committee, last month told members at an Asian Football Confederation meeting in Tokyo that “daily life is ongoing in Saudi Arabia,” despite the regional hostilities.

Before that meeting, AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa had indicated that the Asian Cup could be postponed by a year if necessary, saying “we can wait until the end of November” to make a decision.”

The month-long tournament was scheduled to feature 24 teams playing matches in eight venues across three cites — Riyadh, Jeddah, and Khobar.

Iran qualified and has been grouped with Syria, China and Kyrgyzstan for the league stage.

Asia's marquee continental club tournament — the AFC Champions League Elite — has been disrupted by the conflict.

A game between Cristiano Ronaldo ’s Al-Nassr and Uzbekistan’s Neftchi Fergana was delayed on October 12 after Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence issued a security alert.

An Al-Nassr’s home game in Riyadh last week against Al-Wasl of the United Arab Emirates was postponed because the visiting team didn't travel.

Among other major sports events that have been moved or cancelled in Saudi are the WTA Finals, the season-ending event in women’s tennis, which moved from Riyadh to Indian Wells, California. (AP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Financial institutions laud HK's gateway guardianship
articles.excerpt: Global bank leaders have lauded Hong Kong for its role as a gateway between the mainland and the rest of…
articles.fullText:
Global bank leaders have lauded Hong Kong for its role as a gateway between the mainland and the rest of the world, facilitating two-way financial flows and minimising risks in an era of uncertainty.

At a panel meeting held at the Global Financial Leaders’ Investment Summit in Central, State Street chairman and chief executive Ronald O’Hanley noted that trade patterns had changed in recent years due to uncertainties brought by the pandemic and global conflicts.

More borrowers and people looking to raise capital, he said, are looking for safer options when building supply chains and structuring financing – switching from “just in time to just in case”.

“Where we’re seeing the most change is around the role of China, and Hong Kong is the gateway to that,” O’Hanley said.

"It’s the kind of movement of money north and south and movement of capital north and south, and Hong Kong is playing that role.”

Barclays group chief executive C S Venkatakrishnan said firms had been reducing their dependency on strategic imports over the past decade and that the city which is positioned as both an international financial centre as well as a domestic one is the one that can help countries manage the dependencies.

“I think in order for international finance not to get caught up in the strategic breakdown of dependence, it’s important for the international financial centres like Hong Kong to do what you’re doing – which is to have fair and transparent regulation to promote growth and to make it easy for people to operate,” he said.

BNP Paribas chairman Jean Lemierre noted that more mainland firms were operating in Europe.

With Hong Kong being a renminbi hub, it acts as a bridge between China and Europe that helps these companies gain access to the euro, he said, adding that mainland firms can have better understanding of the European market through the SAR.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Patience pays off at Melbourne Cup for Point Of Law
articles.excerpt: Point Of Law ran down surprise leader Royal Supremacy on the home straight to win the 166th running of the…
articles.fullText:
